Immune Response: Humoral and cellular immune responses assessed; highest responses with S19 and SPEBA with DDA + TDM
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the adjuvant effects on immune responses to a soluble protein extract of Brucella abortus.

Title: Cytokine responses in camels (Camelus bactrianus) vaccinated with Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: cytokine response analysis using real-time PCR assay
Immune Response: upregulation of IFN-gamma and IL-6; low expression of IL-1alpha, IL-1beta, TNFalpha, and IL-10; no expression of IL-2 and IL-4
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the cytokine responses in camels vaccinated with the live attenuated Brucella abortus S19 vaccine.

Title: Brucella melitensis B115-based complement fixation test to detect antibodies induced by Brucella rough strains.
Vaccine Introduction: The study assesses the use of Brucella melitensis B115 as an antigen in a complement fixation test to detect antibodies induced by rough Brucella strains.

Title: The effects of adjuvants on immune responses in cattle injected with a Brucella abortus soluble antigen.
Adjuvant: Muramyl dipeptide, Freund's incomplete adjuvant, dimethyl-dioctadecyl ammonium bromide (DDA), Bordetella pertussis, Propionibacterium acnes
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immune response evaluation through antibody and CMI response measurement
Vaccine Efficacy: Antibody responses significantly higher in immunized steers than controls
Immune Response: Increased CMI responses, particularly with DDA adjuvant
Vaccine Introduction: The study examined the effects of various adjuvants on immune responses to a Brucella abortus soluble antigen in cattle.

Title: Improved performance of Brucella melitensis native hapten over Brucella abortus OPS tracer on goat antibody detection by the fluorescence polarization assay.
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the use of a native hapten from the Rev. 1 strain of Brucella melitensis for improved antibody detection in goats compared to the Brucella abortus OPS tracer.

Title: Immunization with a single dose of a microencapsulated Brucella melitensis mutant enhances protection against wild-type challenge.
Vaccine Efficacy: improved protection against wild-type B. melitensis 16M challenge
Immune Response: elevated Immunoglobulin G levels, increased gamma interferon and interleukin-12 secretion, no interleukin-4
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates a microencapsulated live Brucella melitensis attenuated mutant for its efficacy and immunogenicity compared to a nonencapsulated strain.

Title: A study on the use of male animal models for developing a live vaccine for brucellosis.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: comparison of infection course with virulent strain 16M
Vaccine Efficacy: lower intensity and shorter duration of infection compared to virulent 16M
Immune Response: no inflammation in testis and epididymis following WR201 immunization
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the safety of the live vaccine candidate Brucella melitensis WR201 in male animal models.

Title: Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine: immune response after calfhood vaccination and field investigation in Italian cattle population.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immune response measurement and field investigation
Vaccine Efficacy: Antibody levels increased post-vaccination but decreased over time; 100% sensitivity at days 13 and 14 pv
Immune Response: Antibody levels remained constant for two months post-vaccination
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the immune response to the Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine in cattle and its implications for identifying vaccinated animals in the field.

Title: Immunopathological responses and kinetics of Brucella melitensis Rev 1 infection after subcutaneous or conjunctival vaccination in rams.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: serological studies, pathological and bacteriological examinations
Vaccine Efficacy: fully cleared by 3 months after vaccination
Immune Response: cellular hyperplasia in lymph nodes, lower intensity and duration of response after conjunctival inoculation
Vaccine Introduction: The study assesses the innocuousness of the Brucella melitensis Rev 1 live attenuated vaccine strain in rams, comparing subcutaneous and conjunctival vaccination routes.

Title: [Phenol-insoluble vaccine against human brucellosis: evaluation of the immunogenic power in guinea pigs].
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Comparative study with challenge against virulent Brucella abortus strain 2308
Vaccine Introduction: Living attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 and B. melitensis Rev. 1 were included in the experiment for comparison.

Title: Ultraviolet C lethal effect on Brucella melitensis.
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the sensitivity of the vaccinal strain Rev.1 to UVC radiation compared to wild strains of Brucella melitensis.

Title: Expression of Babesia bovis rhoptry-associated protein 1 (RAP1) in Brucella abortus S19.
Immune Response: strong humoral and cellular immune response
Vaccine Introduction: The study explores the use of Brucella abortus S19 as a vector for expressing heterologous antigens, specifically RAP1 from Babesia bovis, to enhance immunogenicity for combined vaccines against babesiosis and brucellosis.

Title: Genome sequence of Brucella abortus vaccine strain S19 compared to virulent strains yields candidate virulence genes.
Vaccine Introduction: The Brucella abortus strain S19 has been used as a vaccine strain in vaccination of cattle against brucellosis for six decades.

Title: Prevalence of Brucella abortus antibodies in serum of Holstein cattle in Cameroon.
Vaccine Introduction: Vaccination against Brucella abortus should be instituted.

Title: Protection levels in vaccinated heifers with experimental vaccines Brucella abortus M1-luc and INTA 2.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Challenge with virulent B. abortus S2308
Vaccine Introduction: The study also mentions Brucella abortus I2, a double mutant derived from M1-luc, which showed 45.5% protection against abortion.

Title: Incidence of human brucellosis in a rural area in Western Greece after the implementation of a vaccination programme against animal brucellosis.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Incidence rate comparison before and after vaccination
Vaccine Efficacy: Statistically significant decline in human brucellosis incidence
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the implementation of a vaccination programme against animal brucellosis using B. melitensis Rev-1.

Title: [ALL 98 strains of Brucella OMP25 gene is conservative in China].
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: PCR analysis and sequencing of OMP25 gene
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the genetic polymorphism of the OMP25 gene in Brucella strains, which may contribute to vaccine development.

Title: Evaluation of Brucella melitensis B115 as rough-phenotype vaccine against B. melitensis and B. ovis infections.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: protective activity evaluation against B. melitensis and B. ovis infections
Vaccine Efficacy: significant protective immunity against B. melitensis 16M and B. ovis challenge strains
Immune Response: humoral response evaluated; no interfering antibodies to O-PS detected
Vaccine Introduction: Brucella melitensis strain Rev1 is used as vaccine for the prophylaxis of brucellosis in sheep and goats. Alternative vaccines could be live, attenuated Brucella rough strains, which are devoid of the O-PS.

Title: Escheriosomes entrapped DNA vaccine co-expressing Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase and IL-18 confers protection against Brucella abortus.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immunization schedule and immune response assessment
Vaccine Efficacy: Induced SOD specific humoral and cellular immune responses
Immune Response: Higher lymphoproliferative response and IFN-gamma production; IgG2a type antibody response
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates a liposome-based DNA vaccine co-expressing SOD and IL-18 against Brucella abortus.

Title: Brucellosis vaccines: assessment of Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide rough mutants defective in core and O-polysaccharide synthesis and export.
Vaccine Efficacy: Not equal to Rev 1 in laboratory models; two mutants matched protection at higher doses
Vaccine Introduction: Brucella melitensis Rev 1 is a vaccine effective against brucellosis in sheep and goats, but rough mutants lacking O-polysaccharide have been proposed as alternatives.

Title: Evaluation of a multiplex PCR assay (Bruce-ladder) for molecular typing of all Brucella species, including the vaccine strains.
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates a multiplex PCR assay that can differentiate all classical Brucella species, including vaccine strains.

Title: Occupational infection due to Brucella abortus S19 among workers involved in vaccine production in Argentina.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Evaluation of pathological consequences of exposure
Vaccine Introduction: The study reports on the occupational infection due to the vaccine strain Brucella abortus S19 among workers in vaccine production.

Title: [The morphological characteristics of globulin production during the vaccinal process induced by tularemia and brucellosis vaccines].
Immune Response: dynamics of globulin production and antibody titers
Vaccine Introduction: The study also mentions a vaccine for Francisella tularensis.

Title: Seroprevalence of brucellosis in yaks (Poephagus grunniens) in India and evaluation of protective immunity to S19 vaccine.
Vaccine Efficacy: Protective antibody level persisted up to 210 days
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the immune response in yaks following vaccination with Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine and reports on the seroprevalence of brucellosis in yaks in India.

Title: Comparison of heat shock response in Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis.
Vaccine Introduction: The study suggests that hsp-60 can be a good antigenic candidate for engineering a subunit vaccine against Brucella.

Title: Brucellosis with chronic hepatosplenoid form of chronic evolution in a 6-year-old child; Histological study of hepatic lesions after biopsy puncture; involution following two intravenous injections of specific vaccine.
Vaccine Introduction: Specific vaccine administered intravenously.

Title: Effect of polymyxin B and environmental conditions on isolation of Brucella species and the vaccine strain RB51.
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the vaccine strain RB51 among other Brucella species in relation to susceptibility to polymyxin B and environmental conditions.

Title: Brucella abortus strain RB51 leucine auxotroph as an environmentally safe vaccine for plasmid maintenance and antigen overexpression.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Protection against virulent B. abortus 2308 and elicitation of GFP antibodies
Vaccine Efficacy: Protected CD1 mice from virulent B. abortus 2308
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: The differentiation of cattle with Brucella abortus infection titers and cattle vaccinated with Brucella abortus strain 19.
Vaccine Introduction: The study differentiates between cattle infected with Brucella abortus and those vaccinated with Brucella abortus strain 19.

Title: Vaccination of pigs with Brucella abortus vaccine strain 19.
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Lyophilized (desiccated) Brucella abortus vaccine (strain 19).
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Brucella spp. lumazine synthase as a bovine rotavirus antigen delivery system.
Gene or Protein Antigen: BLS (Brucella spp. lumazine synthase), VP8d (bovine rotavirus core protein)
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates BLS as an antigen delivery system to enhance the immunogenicity of rotavirus antigens.

Title: Evaluation of three different antigens in an indirect enzyme-linked immunoassay for the detection of antibodies against Brucella abortus SRB51 in vaccinated heifers.
Vaccine Formulation: 2 ml of a commercially available SRB51 vaccine containing 1x10(7) to 3.4x10(7) viable cells
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Indirect enzyme-linked immunoassay for detecting SRB51 antibodies
Immune Response: All sera samples were negative in the BPA test and in the standard I-ELISA using the SLPS
Vaccine Introduction: The live attenuated Brucella abortus SRB51 (SRB51) is a partial O-chain-deprived mutant.

Title: Stability of poly(epsilon-caprolactone) microparticles containing Brucella ovis antigens as a vaccine delivery system against brucellosis.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Brucella ovis antigenic extract in PEC microparticles
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the use of subcellular vaccines based on poly(epsilon-caprolactone) microparticles containing an antigenic extract of Brucella ovis against experimental brucellosis.

Title: Efficacy of bp26 and bp26/omp31 B. melitensis Rev.1 deletion mutants against Brucella ovis in rams.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Comparison of protection against B. ovis
Vaccine Introduction: Brucella melitensis Rev.1 is the most effective vaccine against B. ovis infection in sheep but induces antibodies interfering with B. melitensis diagnosis.

Title: Immunization with recombinant Brucella species outer membrane protein Omp16 or Omp19 in adjuvant induces specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells as well as systemic and oral protection against Brucella abortus infection.
Vaccine Formulation: incomplete Freund's adjuvant (IFA), aluminum hydroxide, cholera toxin adjuvant
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: flow cytometric analysis, in vivo depletion of CD4(+) or CD8(+) T cells
Vaccine Efficacy: significant protection against B. abortus infection
Immune Response: T helper 1 response, CD4(+) and CD8(+) T cells producing gamma interferon
Vaccine Introduction: The study assessed the use of outer membrane proteins Omp16 and Omp19 as vaccines against Brucella in BALB/c mice, comparing their efficacy to live attenuated strains.

Title: Differentiation by western blotting of immune responses of cattle vaccinated with Brucella abortus strain 19 or infected experimentally or naturally with virulent Brucella abortus.
Immune Response: Detection of bovine immunoglobulin G antibodies
Vaccine Introduction: The study compares immune responses of cattle vaccinated with Brucella abortus strain 19 and those infected with virulent Brucella abortus.

Title: Unresponsiveness of vaccinated BALB/c mice to a second inoculation of lipopolysaccharide from Brucella abortus strain 2308.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Protection against virulent culture of B. abortus strain 2308
Vaccine Efficacy: Vaccinated mice were significantly better protected than nonvaccinated mice
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the protective response of mice vaccinated with lipopolysaccharide from Brucella abortus.

Title: The Brucella abortus S19 DeltavjbR live vaccine candidate is safer than S19 and confers protection against wild-type challenge in BALB/c mice when delivered in a sustained-release vehicle.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: immunogenicity, safety, and protective efficacy evaluation
Vaccine Efficacy: conferred higher levels of protection compared to the nonencapsulated vaccine
Immune Response: elicited an anti-Brucella-specific immunoglobulin G response
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates a vjbR knockout in the S19 vaccine as an improved candidate, addressing drawbacks of existing vaccines like S19 and RB51.

Title: Brucella abortus in Bison. II. Evaluation of strain 19 vaccination of pregnant cows.
Vaccine Formulation: Lyophilized S19 in absorbable hollow pellet
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Manual and ballistic inoculation in pregnant bison
Vaccine Efficacy: 67% protection against abortion; 39% protection against infection
Immune Response: Positive antibody titers in 73% of bison 10 months post-vaccination
Vaccine Introduction: Other methods of vaccination were also evaluated, including manual injection and ballistic inoculation.

Title: Establishment of dose-response relationships in BALB/c mice, using Brucella cell surface protein and lipopolysaccharide.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Brucella cell surface protein (BCSP) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)
Vaccine Efficacy: reduced colony-forming units in vaccinated mice
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the immune and protective responses induced by Brucella cell surface protein and lipopolysaccharide in mice.

Title: Swine immunity to an attenuated Salmonella typhimurium mutant containing a recombinant plasmid which codes for production of a 31-kilodalton protein of Brucella abortus.
Vaccine Efficacy: Stimulated mucosal and systemic antibody-mediated immunity
Immune Response: Serum and intestinal antibody responses; no delayed-type hypersensitivity to recombinant BCSP31
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the use of an attenuated Salmonella typhimurium mutant as a carrier for a Brucella abortus protein to elicit immune responses in swine.

Title: Milk production increase in a dairy farm under a six-year Brucellosis control program.
Vaccine Introduction: Cows were vaccinated as calves with Brucella abortus RB51 and revaccinated annually with a reduced dose.

Title: Evaluation of recombinant invasive, non-pathogenic Eschericia coli as a vaccine vector against the intracellular pathogen, Brucella.
Lab Model or Cell: In vitro and in vivo models
Vaccine Introduction: Live attenuated Brucella strains are widely used to vaccinate animals, but they can cause disease and are unsafe for humans. Killed Brucella or subunit vaccines are not effective in eliciting long-term protection.

Title: Analysis of the occurrence and distribution of the Omp25/Omp31 family of surface proteins in the six classical Brucella species.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the potential interest of Omp25c and Omp31b as subcellular vaccines based on their occurrence in Brucella strains and antigenic relatedness with other proteins.

Title: Immune responses and protection against experimental challenge after vaccination of bison with Brucella abortus strain RB51 or RB51 overexpressing superoxide dismutase and glycosyltransferase genes.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immunologic responses and protection against experimental challenge
Vaccine Efficacy: Greater protection from abortion and infection compared to nonvaccinates
Immune Response: Greater antibody responses, proliferative responses, and production of gamma interferon
Vaccine Introduction: The study also investigates a recombinant RB51 strain overexpressing superoxide dismutase and glycosyltransferase genes (RB51+sodC,wboA).

Title: Cloning, expression and immunogenicity of the translation initiation factor 3 homologue of Brucella abortus.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: in vitro stimulation of lymphoid cells
Vaccine Efficacy: strong proliferative response with gamma interferon production
Vaccine Introduction: The study reports the immunoprotective capacity of the Brucella IF3 protein and proposes it as a promising candidate antigen for subunit vaccines against Brucella.

Title: Vaccination with recombinant Semliki Forest virus particles expressing translation initiation factor 3 of Brucella abortus induces protective immunity in BALB/c mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immune response evaluation and challenge with B. abortus 2308
Vaccine Efficacy: Significant level of resistance against challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308 (P<0.01)
Immune Response: Induction of IF3-specific IgM antibodies, T-cell proliferative response, and interferon gamma secretion
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the potential of SFV-IF3 as a vaccine to induce protection against B. abortus infections.

Title: Enhanced immune response of red deer (Cervus elaphus) to live rb51 vaccine strain using composite microspheres.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: oral and subcutaneous vaccination, challenge with B. abortus strain 19
Vaccine Efficacy: significant reduction in bacterial counts in spleens
Immune Response: anti-Brucella specific IgG response, cell-mediated response
Vaccine Introduction: The current vaccine used for cattle Brucella abortus strain RB51 has proven ineffective in protecting bison and elk from infection and abortion.

Title: Rough mutants defective in core and O-polysaccharide synthesis and export induce antibodies reacting in an indirect ELISA with smooth lipopolysaccharide and are less effective than Rev 1 vaccine against Brucella melitensis infection of sheep.
Vaccine Introduction: Reference B. melitensis Rev 1 vaccine was used for comparison.

Title: The profile of cytokines and IgG subclasses in BALB/c mice after immunization with Brucella ribosomal gene.
Vaccine Efficacy: Lower bacterial cfu from vaccinated mice compared to control groups
Immune Response: High levels of IFNgamma, low levels of IL-5, high IgG2a/IgG1 ratio indicating Th1 response
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Immunogencity of HSA-L7/L12 (Brucella abortus ribosomal protein) in an animal model.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: ELISA, LTT test, bacterial counts from spleens
Vaccine Efficacy: significant protection against challenge with virulent strain B. abortus 544
Immune Response: strong T-cell proliferative response, dominance of IgG1 over IgG2a
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the immunogenicity of the tHSA-L7/L12 fusion protein as a candidate for subunit vaccines against brucellosis.

Title: Development and characterization of mouse models of infection with aerosolized Brucella melitensis and Brucella suis.
Extracted Vaccine Name: live B. melitensis vaccine strain Rev.1
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: evaluation of vaccines using mouse models
Vaccine Introduction: The study focuses on the evaluation of the live B. melitensis vaccine strain Rev.1 in mouse models of infection with aerosolized Brucella.

Title: A combined DNA vaccine provides protective immunity against Mycobacterium bovis and Brucella abortus in cattle.
Vaccine Efficacy: Significantly reduced bacterial counts and improved immune responses compared to controls
Immune Response: Stronger antigen-specific IFN-gamma responses and higher IgG titers
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates a combined DNA vaccine targeting both Mycobacterium bovis and Brucella abortus.

Title: Experimental infection of Richardson's ground squirrels (Spermophilus richardsonii) with attenuated and virulent strains of Brucella abortus.
Vaccine Efficacy: Some persistence of bacteria detected, but no evidence of pathology
Vaccine Introduction: The study also involved B. abortus strain 19 (s19) and virulent B. abortus strain 9941 (s9941) for comparison.

Title: Shedding of Brucella abortus rough mutant strain RB51 in milk of water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis).
Extracted Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus rough mutant strain RB51
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: isolation of SRB51 from milk samples and PCR analysis
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the shedding of the Brucella abortus rough mutant strain RB51 in the milk of vaccinated water buffaloes.

Title: Deletion of the BCSP31 gene of Brucella abortus by replacement.
Lab Model or Cell: J774 macrophage-like cell line, HeLa cells
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Gene deletion and antibiotic resistance confirmation
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the deletion of the BCSP31 gene in B. abortus strains, including the vaccine strain B. abortus S19 used for preventing bovine brucellosis.

Title: Simultaneous expression of homologous and heterologous antigens in rough, attenuated Brucella melitensis.
Gene or Protein Antigen: wboA gene (Brucella) and pag gene (Bacillus anthracis)
Vaccine Formulation: Plasmid pBBR4MCS introduced into O-antigen deficient B. melitensis strain WRRP1
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Induced protection against challenge with B. melitensis strain 16M
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the expression of homologous and heterologous antigens in an attenuated Brucella melitensis strain.

Title: Design and influence of gamma-irradiation on the biopharmaceutical properties of nanoparticles containing an antigenic complex from Brucella ovis.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Brucella ovis antigenic extract (HS) in nanoparticles
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Pharmacopoeial biological tests and gamma-irradiation effects
Vaccine Efficacy: Suggestive for use in brucellosis immunoprophylaxis
Vaccine Introduction: This work describes the development of a novel formulation strategy to the delivery of the Brucella ovis antigenic extract into ovine mucosal surfaces.

Title: Eradication of bovine brucellosis in the Azores, Portugal-Outcome of a 5-year programme (2002-2007) based on test-and-slaughter and RB51 vaccination.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Eradication programme based on mass vaccination and test-and-slaughter
Vaccine Efficacy: Average herd incidence decreased by 69.26%, herd prevalence by 39.26%, and individual prevalence by 75.41%
Vaccine Introduction: The study reports on the use of the RB51 vaccine in a mass vaccination programme combined with test-and-slaughter to control bovine brucellosis in the Azores.

Title: Characterization of possible correlates of protective response against Brucella ovis infection in rams immunized with the B. melitensis Rev 1 vaccine.
Immune Response: characterization of inflammatory and immune response genes
Vaccine Introduction: The study focuses on the B. melitensis Rev 1 vaccine used to control ovine brucellosis caused by Brucella ovis in sheep.

Title: Protection of mice from Brucella infection by immunization with attenuated Salmonella enterica serovar typhimurium expressing A L7/L12 and BLS fusion antigen of Brucella.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Comparison of immunogenicity and protective efficacy
Vaccine Efficacy: Elicited mucosal and systemic immunity, protection against B. abortus 544 infection
Immune Response: Induced humoral and cellular immune responses, but not mucosal immunity for rBL and pBL
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the use of attenuated Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium expressing Brucella antigens as a vaccination strategy against Brucella infection.

Title: Immunogenic mimics of Brucella lipopolysaccharide epitopes.
Vaccine Introduction: The study developed peptides mimicking antigenic properties of Brucella LPS for potential vaccine design.

Title: [Construction of BP26 tagged vaccine strain and development of discriminating PCR for Brucella].
Vaccine Efficacy: Decreased infection capability compared to wild type strain
Vaccine Introduction: A new tagged strain, M5DeltaBP26, was successfully constructed to prevent drawbacks of live attenuated vaccine strains.

Title: Nondividing but metabolically active gamma-irradiated Brucella melitensis is protective against virulent B. melitensis challenge in mice.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the use of gamma-irradiated Brucella melitensis as a nonliving vaccine that retains protective features while being nonvirulent.

Title: Efficacy of strain RB51 vaccine in protecting infection and vertical transmission against Brucella abortus in Sprague-Dawley rats.
Vaccine Introduction: This study evaluates the effectiveness of the B. abortus strain RB51 vaccine in protecting against infection and vertical transmission in Sprague-Dawley rats.

Title: Caspase-2 mediated apoptotic and necrotic murine macrophage cell death induced by rough Brucella abortus.
Lab Model or Cell: RAW264.7 macrophages, bone marrow derived macrophages, primary mouse peritoneal macrophages
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Induction of apoptotic and necrotic cell death in macrophages
Immune Response: Induction of caspase-2 mediated macrophage cell death
Vaccine Introduction: B. abortus vaccine strain RB51 is an attenuated rough, lipopolysaccharide O antigen-deficient mutant derived from smooth strain 2308.

Title: The polymeric antigen BLSOmp31 confers protection against Brucella ovis infection in rams.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immunization of rams with different formulations and adjuvants
Vaccine Efficacy: 76% protection with prime-boost strategy, 63% with chimera rBLSOmp31 in IFA
Immune Response: Induced high levels of IgG specific antibodies with bacteriolytic activity and specific IFN-gamma
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the polymeric vaccine BLSOmp31 targeting Brucella ovis, highlighting its potential as a vaccine against ovine brucellosis.

Title: Diagnostic efficacy of Brucella abortus strain RB51 in experimentally inoculated Sprague-Dawley rats using western blot assay.

Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the efficacy of Brucella abortus strain RB51 in inducing an immune response in Sprague-Dawley rats.

Title: Immune responses and efficacy after administration of a commercial Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine to cattle.
Vaccine Efficacy: Highly efficacious in preventing Brucella-induced abortion or fetal infection
Immune Response: Greater antibody responses and lymphocyte proliferative responses in vaccinated cattle
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the immunologic responses and efficacy of the commercial Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine in cattle against brucellosis.

Title: Expression of human serum albumin--L7/L12 (Brucella abortus ribosomal protein) fusion protein in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Expression and purification of fusion protein
Vaccine Introduction: The immunogenic B. abortus ribosomal protein L7/L12 is a promising candidate antigen for the development of subunit vaccines against brucellosis.

Title: [Combined vaccines including 1 or several anti-foot-and-mouth valences].
Vaccine Formulation: classical aqueous vaccines in aluminum hydroxide, emulsified vaccines containing oily adjuvants
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the combination of anti-brucella vaccines with other vaccines, particularly in the context of combined vaccines for foot-and-mouth disease and rabies.

Title: Discordant Brucella melitensis antigens yield cognate CD8+ T cells in vivo.

Immune Response: Gamma interferon production by CD8+ T cells
Vaccine Introduction: Recent work has advanced the field of Brucella vaccine development, but there remains no safe human vaccine.

Title: [Preliminary study of the combination of anti-foot-and-mouth disease and anti-brucellosis vaccines].
Vaccine Efficacy: results obtained with combined vaccine are identical with those obtained with each of the monovalent vaccines
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates a combined vaccine using Brucella B19 strain as an adjuvant in the context of foot-and-mouth disease vaccination.

Title: Evaluation of particulate acellular vaccines against Brucella ovis infection in rams.

Vaccine Introduction: The attenuated Brucella melitensis Rev 1 vaccine has drawbacks, leading to the development of acellular vaccines based on a Brucella ovis antigenic complex.

Title: Oral vaccination with microencapsuled strain 19 vaccine confers enhanced protection against Brucella abortus strain 2308 challenge in red deer (Cervus elaphus elaphus).
Vaccine Efficacy: Statistically significant lower bacterial tissue load compared with controls
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated Strain 19 (S19) in a sustained release vehicle suitable for wildlife, indicating a potential improvement for Brucella-vaccine delivery.

Title: Identification of Brucella abortus genes in elk (Cervus elaphus) using in vivo-induced antigen technology (IVIAT) reveals novel markers of infection.

Vaccine Introduction: The study identifies novel B. abortus antigens and their immune responses in elk, but does not focus on a specific vaccine.

Title: Eradication of bovine brucellosis in the Azores, Portugal--outcome of a 5-year programme (2002-2007) based on test-and-slaughter and RB51 vaccination.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the use of RB51 vaccination as part of a test-and-slaughter program for the eradication of bovine brucellosis.

Title: DeltaznuADeltapurE Brucella abortus 2308 mutant as a live vaccine candidate.

Title: Relationship of strain 19 calfhood vaccination in beef herds and brucellosis reactor rates, duration of quarantine, and number of herd tests.

Vaccine Introduction: The study analyzes the potential of the P39 antigen as a vaccine against B. melitensis 16 M infection.

Title: Protection of mice against Brucella abortus 544 challenge by vaccination with recombinant OMP28 adjuvanted with CpG oligonucleotides.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: systemic bacterial clearance after challenge with B. abortus 544
Vaccine Efficacy: significant protection but lower than required level
Immune Response: vigorous IgG response, increased cell mediated immune response, biased towards Th1 type

Title: Bovine brucellosis.
Vaccine Introduction: Other vaccine studied: B abortus strain RB51.

Title: Comparative study of gamma interferon production in mice immunized with outer membrane proteins and whole bacteria of Brucella abortus.

Vaccine Efficacy: Enhanced antibody, proliferative T cell, and IFN-γ responses
Vaccine Introduction: Current livestock B. abortus vaccines have not proven to be efficacious in bison or elk.

Title: Protective efficacy and safety of Brucella melitensis 16MΔmucR against intraperitoneal and aerosol challenge in BALB/c mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: protective efficacy and safety evaluation against intraperitoneal and aerosol challenge
Vaccine Efficacy: statistically significant degree of protection against both intraperitoneal and aerosol challenge
Vaccine Introduction: Currently licensed vaccine strains used in animals are unacceptable for human use due to undesirable side effects and modest protection. Substantial progress has been made during the past 10 years toward the development of improved vaccines for brucellosis.

Title: Protective live oral brucellosis vaccines stimulate Th1 and th17 cell responses.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Nasal challenge with wild-type B. melitensis 16M
Vaccine Efficacy: 83% of vaccinated mice had no detectable brucellae in spleens
Vaccine Introduction: The study focuses on a live oral brucellosis vaccine, ΔznuA B. melitensis, which has shown protective effects against nasal challenges with virulent B. melitensis.

Title: Preliminary assessment of binary ethylenimine inactivated and saponized cutaneous warts (BPV-2) therapeutic vaccine for enzootic bovine haematuria in hill cows.
Vaccine Efficacy: Failed to show favorable clinical results
Immune Response: Encouraging humoral and cell-mediated immune responses
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated a therapeutic vaccine for enzootic bovine haematuria that showed immune responses against Brucella abortus strain 19S.

Title: Ontology-based Brucella vaccine literature indexing and systematic analysis of gene-vaccine association network.
Vaccine Introduction: The study examined vaccines for Brucella, the causative agent of brucellosis in humans and animals.

Title: Evaluation of the recombinant 10-kilodalton immunodominant region of the BP26 protein of Brucella abortus for specific diagnosis of bovine brucellosis.
Vaccine Introduction: The study focuses on the use of a recombinant 10-kDa protein of B. abortus for specific diagnosis of bovine brucellosis, rather than a vaccine.

Title: Immunoproteomic analysis of Brucella melitensis and identification of a new immunogenic candidate protein for the development of brucellosis subunit vaccine.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: immunoproteomic assay, in vitro stimulation, bacterial challenge
Vaccine Efficacy: partially protected against B. melitensis infection
Vaccine Introduction: LS-2 is an already well-known vaccine candidate; the study focuses on the novel vaccine candidate RS-α.

Title: Identification of immunoreactive proteins of Brucella melitensis by immunoproteomics.
Gene or Protein Antigen: elongation factor G, F0F1 ATP synthase subunit beta, OMP1
Vaccine Introduction: The study identifies novel candidate immunogenic proteins from Brucella melitensis M5 for potential vaccine development.

Title: Comparison of abortion and infection after experimental challenge of pregnant bison and cattle with Brucella abortus strain 2308.
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Herd prevalence of bovine brucellosis and analysis of risk factors in cattle in urban and peri-urban areas of the Kampala economic zone, Uganda.
Vaccine Introduction: Vaccination should be targeted at commercial large-scale farms with free-grazing farming to control brucellosis in cattle in and around Kampala city.

Title: Molecular typing of Brucella melitensis endemic strains and differentiation from the vaccine strain Rev-1.
Vaccine Introduction: The study focuses on differentiating the endemic strains of Br. melitensis from the vaccine strain Rev-1 using molecular typing techniques.

Title: Antigenic, immunologic and genetic characterization of rough strains B. abortus RB51, B. melitensis B115 and B. melitensis B18.
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated rough strains B. abortus RB51, B. melitensis B115, and B. melitensis B18 as potential brucellosis vaccines due to their favorable features and lower virulence compared to wild type strains.

Title: The interaction of Brucella melitensis 16-M and caprine polymorphonuclear leukocytes.
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Representative seroprevalences of brucellosis in humans and livestock in Kyrgyzstan.
Vaccine Introduction: mass vaccination of sheep and goats but also of cattle

Title: Extended safety and efficacy studies of the attenuated Brucella vaccine candidates 16 M(Delta)vjbR and S19(Delta)vjbR in the immunocompromised IRF-1-/- mouse model.
Vaccine Efficacy: significantly reduced colonization in multiple organs
Vaccine Introduction: The study also mentions the vaccine candidate S19ΔvjbR, which is a live attenuated vaccine for human and animal use.

Title: Oral immunization of mice with recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing Cu,Zn superoxide dismutase of Brucella abortus triggers protective immunity.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Lactococcus lactis expressing Cu,Zn superoxide dismutase
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Oral vaccination and challenge with virulent B. abortus 2308 strain
Vaccine Efficacy: Protected against challenge with virulent B. abortus 2308 strain
Immune Response: Induction of anti-SOD-specific IgM and IgG responses, SOD-specific sIgA, and T-cell-proliferative responses
Vaccine Introduction: Evaluated the usefulness of recombinant Lactococcus lactis secreting Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase as an oral antigen delivery system.

Title: Immunogenic proteins of Brucella abortus to minimize cross reactions in brucellosis diagnosis.
Gene or Protein Antigen: F0F1 ATP synthase subunit β, solute-binding family 5 protein, 28 kDa OMP, Leu/Ile/Val-binding family protein, Histidinol dehydrogenase, Hypothetical protein, Twin-arginine translocation pathway signal sequence domain-containing protein, Dihydroorotase, Serine protease family protein, β-hydroxyacyl-(acyl-carrier-protein) dehydratase FabA, Short-chain dehydrogenase-/reductase carbonic anhydrase, Ornithine carbamoyltransferase, Leucyl aminopeptidase, Cold shock DNA-binding domain-containing protein, Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase, Methionine aminopeptidase
Vaccine Introduction: The study identifies 18 immunogenic proteins of Brucella abortus that can be considered candidate antigens for vaccine development to minimize cross reactions in brucellosis diagnosis.

Title: Deep-sequencing analysis of the mouse transcriptome response to infection with Brucella melitensis strains of differing virulence.
Vaccine Introduction: B. melitensis strain M5-90, a live attenuated vaccine cultured from B. melitensis strain M28, has been used as an effective tool in the control of brucellosis in goats and sheep in China.

Title: Brucellosis control in Tajikistan using Rev 1 vaccine: change in seroprevalence in small ruminants from 2004 to 2009.
Vaccine Efficacy: Seroprevalence dropped by 80% in well-implemented vaccination areas
Immune Response: Vaccinated sheep and goats had higher serotest positivity compared to non-vaccinated
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the efficacy of the Rev 1 vaccine in controlling brucellosis in small ruminants in Tajikistan.

Title: Role of TLRs in Brucella mediated murine DC activation in vitro and clearance of pulmonary infection in vivo.
Lab Model or Cell: Bone marrow derived dendritic cell model
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Challenge experiments to assess DC activation and function, and clearance of strains in vivo
Vaccine Efficacy: Significant DC activation and protection against pathogenic strain 2308
Immune Response: TLR2 and TLR9 dependent TNF-α production; TLR2 and TLR4 dependent IL-12 production
Vaccine Introduction: Live attenuated Brucella abortus vaccine strain RB51 protects cattle through CD4 and CD8 T-cell mediated responses.

Title: Characterization of outer membrane vesicles from Brucella melitensis and protection induced in mice.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from Brucella melitensis
Gene or Protein Antigen: SOD, GroES, Omp31, Omp25, Omp19, bp26, Omp16
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immunization and challenge with virulent strain B. melitensis 16 M
Vaccine Efficacy: Protected from challenge with virulent strain B. melitensis 16 M
Immune Response: Induced higher expression of IL-12, TNFα, and IFNγ; increased levels of serum IgG2a
Vaccine Introduction: OMVs from smooth B. melitensis 16 M and rough mutant VTRM1 were characterized and shown to induce immune responses in mice.

Title: Serological profile of buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) female calves vaccinated with standard Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine using rose bengal, 2-mercaptoethanol and complement fixation tests.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Serological evaluation using rose bengal, 2-mercaptoethanol, and complement fixation tests
Vaccine Efficacy: Early response observed in CFT; no reactions after 360 days
Immune Response: Above 95% of animals showed reactions in all tests by day 15; absence of reactions at later time points
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the serological profiles of buffalo calves vaccinated with Brucella abortus strain 19.

Title: Serological and bacteriological responses of water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) vaccinated with two doses of Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine.
Vaccine Efficacy: Antibody responses to RB51 were demonstrated in all vaccinates but not in controls
Immune Response: Positive antibody responses detected using CFT and dot-blot assay
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated serological responses to Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccination in water buffalo calves and compared the use of two selective media for isolation of RB51.

Title: Exploiting the Campylobacter jejuni protein glycosylation system for glycoengineering vaccines and diagnostic tools directed against brucellosis.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Glycoprotein derived from Yersinia enterocolitica O9
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: IgG response measurement and challenge with virulent B. abortus strain
Immune Response: Generated an IgG response recognizing the O antigen of Brucella
Vaccine Introduction: The study explores the use of glycoproteins engineered from bacterial glycosylation systems for potential applications in brucellosis diagnostics and vaccines.

Title: Efficacy evaluation of live Escherichia coli expression Brucella P39 protein combined with CpG oligodeoxynucleotides vaccine against Brucella melitensis 16M, in BALB/c mice.
Extracted Vaccine Name: E. coli BL21 (DE3) pEt15b-p39 with CpG ODN
Vaccine Formulation: E. coli BL21 (DE3) pEt15b-p39 with CpG oligodeoxynucleotides
Vaccine Efficacy: Higher level of protection against B. melitensis 16M
Immune Response: Significant IFN-γ production, T-cell proliferation, and antibody responses (IgG, IgG1, IgG2a)
Vaccine Introduction: Other groups included E. coli BL21 (DE3) pEt15b alone or with non-CpG ODN. Rev.1 protection was more effective than the tested vaccine.

Title: Safety and immunogenicity of Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine in cross bred cattle calves in India.

Immune Response: Good IFN-gamma response; 80% of calves showed cumulative IFN-gamma response at 60 days post vaccination
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the safety and immunogenicity of the Brucella abortus RB51 vaccine in cattle calves.

Title: Immunization of mice with recombinant protein CobB or AsnC confers protection against Brucella abortus infection.
Vaccine Efficacy: provided protection against virulent B. abortus infection
Vaccine Introduction: The study focused on screening Brucella protective antigens as subunit vaccine candidates, identifying CobB and AsnC as potential antigens that stimulate T-cell responses and provide protection against brucellosis.

Title: Characterization of periplasmic protein BP26 epitopes of Brucella melitensis reacting with murine monoclonal and sheep antibodies.
Vaccine Efficacy: 65-70% reactivity for linear epitopes; 90% for NMP
Vaccine Introduction: An attenuated B. melitensis vaccine M5-90 is currently used for vaccination of sheep and goats in China.

Title: Immune responses and safety after dart or booster vaccination of bison with Brucella abortus strain RB51.
Vaccine Formulation: 1.1 × 10(10) to 2.0 × 10(10) CFU for hand vaccination; 1.8 × 10(10) CFU for dart vaccination; 2.2 × 10(10) CFU for booster vaccination
Vaccine Efficacy: Greater serologic responses in booster-vaccinated bison compared to single vaccinates
Immune Response: Greater gamma interferon (IFN-γ) production in booster vaccinates; reduced antigen-specific proliferative responses compared to single vaccinates
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the effects of dart and booster vaccinations with Brucella abortus strain RB51 in bison, focusing on immunologic responses and safety.

Title: Intradermal immunization with outer membrane protein 25 protects Balb/c mice from virulent B. abortus 544.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: immunogenic potential and protective efficacy against virulent B. abortus challenge
Vaccine Efficacy: significant reduction in splenic colonization of B. abortus in immunized mice
Immune Response: mixed Th1 and Th2 type of immune response with elevated levels of IL-12 and IFN-γ
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the immunogenic potential of recombinant Omp25 and its protective efficacy against virulent B. abortus in Balb/c mice.

Title: Chaperonin GroEL a Brucella immunodominant antigen identified using Nanobody and MALDI-TOF-MS technologies.
Vaccine Introduction: The study focuses on the identification of new immunogenic proteins of Brucella, specifically the chaperonin GroEL, which is an immunodominant antigen.

Title: Immunoproteomics of Brucella abortus reveals differential antibody profiles between S19-vaccinated and naturally infected cattle.
Gene or Protein Antigen: Invasion protein B, Sod, Dps, Ndk, Bfr

Vaccine Introduction: The study characterizes a B. abortus S19 antigen preparation and differentiates between infected and vaccinated cattle.

Title: Protective role of antibodies induced by Brucella melitensis B115 against B. melitensis and Brucella abortus infections in mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Evaluation of protective ability of specific antisera
Immune Response: Antibodies induced by B115 act as opsonins
Vaccine Introduction: The study compares the protective ability of antibodies induced by B. melitensis B115 with those from B. abortus RB51 and S19 strains.

Title: Efficacy of dart or booster vaccination with strain RB51 in protecting bison against experimental Brucella abortus challenge.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Comparison of vaccination methods (single intramuscular, pneumatic dart, and booster)
Vaccine Efficacy: Reduced incidence of abortion and infection in bison
Immune Response: Enhanced protective immunity with booster vaccination
Vaccine Introduction: The study compares the efficacy of different delivery methods of the RB51 vaccine in bison against Brucella abortus challenge.

Title: The NtrY/X two-component system of Brucella spp. acts as a redox sensor and regulates the expression of nitrogen respiration enzymes.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the adaptation mechanisms of Brucella spp. and the potential for developing new vaccines against brucellosis.

Title: The lipopolysaccharide core of Brucella abortus acts as a shield against innate immunity recognition.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Proinflammatory response induction and dendritic cell maturation

Title: Recombinant VirB5 protein as a potential serological marker for the diagnosis of bovine brucellosis.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses a gene deletion mutant strain, B. abortus S19 virB5, as a molecular tag vaccine against Brucella abortus.

Title: Identification of Brucella abortus virulence proteins that modulate the host immune response.
Immune Response: increased levels of gamma interferon (IFNγ) in splenocytes
Vaccine Introduction: The study identifies three proteins from Brucella abortus that may serve as potential live, attenuated vaccine candidates due to their role in modulating the host immune response.

Title: Invasive Escherichia coli vaccines expressing Brucella melitensis outer membrane proteins 31 or 16 or periplasmic protein BP26 confer protection in mice challenged with B. melitensis.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Invasive E. coli expressing B. melitensis Omp31 or Omp16 or BP26
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Protection against virulent B. melitensis challenge
Vaccine Efficacy: Induced significant protection against B. melitensis
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the development of alternative vaccines to the current Brucella melitensis Rev.1 vaccine, using recombinant E. coli to express Brucella outer membrane proteins for enhanced protection.

Title: Induction of protective immunity against brucellosis in mice by vaccination with a combination of naloxone, alum, and heat-killed Brucella melitensis 16 M.
Vaccine Formulation: Combination of naloxone, alum, and heat-killed Brucella melitensis 16 M
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Measurement of serum levels of interferon (IFN)-γ, interleukin (IL)-4, bacterial load, and survival rate
Immune Response: Increased serum levels of IFN-γ, IL-4, and immunoglobulin G
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the induction of protective immunity in mice against brucellosis using a combination of naloxone, alum, and heat-killed Brucella melitensis 16 M.

Title: Immunogenicity and protective potential of a bacterially expressed recombinant dihydrolipoamide succinyltransferase (rE2o) of Brucella abortus in BALB/c mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: humoral immune response by ELISA, lymphocyte proliferation assay, cytokine profiling
Vaccine Efficacy: provides partial protection against challenge with pathogenic Brucella abortus
Immune Response: induces a mixed but predominant Th2 type of immune response
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Immunodetection of the recombinant GroEL by the Nanobody NbBruc02.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immunochromatography, ELISA, immunoblotting, surface plasmon resonance (SPR) biosensor
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the development of diagnostics and vaccines for Brucella, focusing on the Nanobody NbBruc02 that targets the Brucella heat shock protein GroEL.

Title: Antigen-specific acquired immunity in human brucellosis: implications for diagnosis, prognosis, and vaccine development.
Vaccine Introduction: Current attenuated Brucella vaccines used in animals cause human disease; there is a need for a recombinant protein subunit vaccine for human brucellosis.

Title: Characterization of recombinant B. abortus strain RB51SOD toward understanding the uncorrelated innate and adaptive immune responses induced by RB51SOD compared to its parent vaccine strain RB51.

Title: Conjunctival vaccination against Brucella ovis in mice with mannosylated nanoparticles.

Title: Vaccination with recombinant flagellar proteins FlgJ and FliN induce protection against Brucella abortus 544 infection in BALB/c mice.

Title: Immunogenic response of Brucella canis virB10 and virB11 mutants in a murine model.

Title: Brucella ovis excretion in semen of seronegative, clinically normal breeding rams.

Vaccine Introduction: Vaccination against B ovis was used in the study.

Title: [Use of multiple locus variable number tandem repeats analysis for the Brucella systematization].
Vaccine Introduction: The study tested two vaccine strains among twenty-six Brucella strains representing reference and field strains.

Title: Caspase-2-dependent dendritic cell death, maturation, and priming of T cells in response to Brucella abortus infection.

Vaccine Efficacy: Induces maturation, activation, and cytokine production in dendritic cells
Immune Response: Stimulates proliferation of CD4(+) and CD8(+) T cells
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the live attenuated rough B. abortus strain RB51, which is a licensed vaccine for cattle, and compares its effects to the virulent smooth strain S2308.

Title: Isolation of a field strain of Brucella abortus from RB51-vaccinated- and brucellosis-seronegative bovine yearlings that calved normally.

Title: Protective effects of recombinant Brucella abortus Omp28 against infection with a virulent strain of Brucella abortus 544 in mice.

Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the immunogenicity and protective ability of recombinant Omp28 against Brucella abortus infection.

Title: Evaluation of protective effect of DNA vaccines encoding the BAB1_0263 and BAB1_0278 open reading frames of Brucella abortus in BALB/c mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Intramuscular injection and immune response evaluation
Vaccine Efficacy: Induced protection against challenge with virulent strain B. abortus 2308
Immune Response: Elicited humoral and cellular immune responses, Th1-dominated immune response
Vaccine Introduction: The study also examined another DNA vaccine, pVF263, which encodes the BAB1_0263 gene.

Title: Crucial role of gamma interferon-producing CD4+ Th1 cells but dispensable function of CD8+ T cell, B cell, Th2, and Th17 responses in the control of Brucella melitensis infection in mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: comparison of lymphocyte subsets in immune control of Brucella infection
Immune Response: key function of gamma interferon (IFN-γ)-producing Th1 CD4(+) T cells
Vaccine Introduction: There is currently no approved vaccine against human brucellosis, and antibiotic therapy is long and costly. Development of a safe protective vaccine requires a better understanding of the roles played by components of adaptive immunity in the control of Brucella infection.

Title: The role of a Brucella abortus lipoprotein in intracellular replication and pathogenicity in experimentally infected mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: infection and recovery of mutants from spleen
Vaccine Efficacy: fewer mutants recovered from spleen compared to wild-type
Vaccine Introduction: The study indicates that the B. abortus lipoprotein mutant may help improve live vaccines used to control brucellosis.

Title: A polymeric protein induces specific cytotoxicity in a TLR4 dependent manner in the absence of adjuvants.

Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses a chimera of lumazine synthase from Brucella spp. that can induce immunity without adjuvants.

Title: Measurement of immunosuppression in chickens caused by infectious bursal disease vaccines using Brucella abortus strain 19.

Title: Genome sequences of three live attenuated vaccine strains of Brucella species and implications for pathogenesis and differential diagnosis.

Title: A combined vaccine against Brucella abortus and infectious bovine rhinotracheitis.

Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates a combined vaccine against Brucella abortus and infectious bovine rhinotracheitis, focusing on immune response in vaccinated calves.

Title: Systematic annotation and analysis of "virmugens"-virulence factors whose mutants can be used as live attenuated vaccines.

Title: [Effects of Brucella phosphoglucomutase on inducing infection of trophoblastic cells].

Immune Response: Increased activity of IL-6, TNF-alpha in infected cells
Vaccine Introduction: The study involves the Brucella pgm mutant and its effects compared to the Brucella vaccine strain M5-90.

Title: Pluronic P85 enhances the efficacy of outer membrane vesicles as a subunit vaccine against Brucella melitensis challenge in mice.

Title: In vivo differences in the virulence, pathogenicity, and induced protective immunity of wboA mutants from genetically different parent Brucella spp.

Title: Ontology representation and analysis of vaccine formulation and administration and their effects on vaccine immune responses.

Title: Evaluation of the effects of erythritol on gene expression in Brucella abortus.

Title: Modeling the transmission dynamics of sheep brucellosis in Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, China.

Title: Immunological responses to recombinant cysteine synthase A of Brucella abortus in BALB/c mice.

Title: Brucella immunogenic BP26 forms a channel-like structure.

Title: Safety and efficacy of reduced doses of Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine in pregnant Iranian fat-tailed ewes.

Title: Cell mediated immune response after challenge in Omp25 liposome immunized mice contributes to protection against virulent Brucella abortus 544.

Title: [Radiolabeling and biodistribution studies of polymeric nanoparticles as adjuvants for ocular vaccination against brucellosis].

Title: Immune reactivity of Brucella melitensis-vaccinated rabbit serum with recombinant Omp31 and DnaK proteins.

Title: Inactivation of the ABC transporter ATPase gene in Brucella abortus strain 2308 attenuated the virulence of the bacteria.

Title: Immune response and serum bactericidal activity against Brucella ovis elicited using a short immunization schedule with the polymeric antigen BLSOmp31 in rams.

Title: Evaluation of the immunogenicity and the protective efficacy in mice of a DNA vaccine encoding SP41 from Brucella melitensis.

Title: Immunogenic and invasive properties of Brucella melitensis 16M outer membrane protein vaccine candidates identified via a reverse vaccinology approach.

Title: Immunogenicity and safety of a natural rough mutant of Brucella suis as a vaccine for swine.
