Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the development of glycoconjugate antigens and conjugate vaccines based on synthetic oligosaccharides targeting Brucella antigens.

Title: Vaccination of adult animals with a reduced dose of Brucella abortus S19 vaccine to control brucellosis on dairy farms in endemic areas of India.
Immune Response: Antibody response vanished within 9 to 12 weeks
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the use of a reduced dose of Brucella abortus S19 vaccine for controlling brucellosis in dairy farms.

Title: Improved immunogenicity of tetanus toxoid by Brucella abortus S19 LPS adjuvant.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Tetanus toxoid with Brucella abortus S19 LPS
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Antibody production measurement and LD50 determination
Vaccine Efficacy: 100% protective effect against TT in immunized mice
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the adjuvant effect of Brucella abortus LPS for tetanus toxoid antigen.

Title: Transmission dynamics and control for a brucellosis model in Hinggan League of Inner Mongolia, China.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses vaccination as one of the strategies for controlling human brucellosis in Hinggan League.

Title: Oral delivery of Brucella spp. recombinant protein U-Omp16 abrogates the IgE-mediated milk allergy.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: oral administration with cow's milk proteins
Immune Response: shift of the balance of Th1- and Th2-T cells toward Th1 predominance
Vaccine Introduction: The unlipidated Omp16 (U-Omp16) is the outer membrane protein of 16 kDa from B. abortus and possesses a mucosal adjuvant property.

Title: Thermostable cross-protective subunit vaccine against Brucella species.
Gene or Protein Antigen: A antigen of Brucella abortus and M antigen of Brucella melitensis
Vaccine Formulation: polysaccharide (PS; >90% [wt/wt]) and a small amount of protein (1 to 3%)
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: challenge with representative strains of B. abortus, B. melitensis, and B. suis
Vaccine Efficacy: protected mice with statistically significant reduction in bacterial colonization
Immune Response: induced serum IgG response to Brucella antigens that remained elevated for up to 9 weeks
Vaccine Introduction: The study presents a subunit vaccine candidate produced from Brucella suis 145, showing cross-protective capabilities against multiple Brucella species.

Title: Evaluation of the efficacy of outer membrane protein 31 vaccine formulations for protection against Brucella canis in BALB/c mice.
Vaccine Formulation: Different adjuvants (incomplete Freund adjuvant, aluminum hydroxide, Quil A, Montanide IMS 3012 VGPR), plasmid pCIOmp31, rOmp31
Adjuvant: Incomplete Freund adjuvant, aluminum hydroxide, Quil A, Montanide IMS 3012 VGPR
Immune Response: Induced strong IgG response, mixed Th1-Th2 response
Vaccine Introduction: Currently, there is no vaccine available against canine brucellosis, and preventive measures are simply diagnosis and isolation of infected dogs.

Title: Mapping of major diseases and devising prevention and control regimen to common diseases in cattle and shoats in Dassenech district of South Omo Zone, South-Western Ethiopia.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the need for vaccination against brucellosis in bovine, suggesting it should be applied at the beginning of the dry season, and emphasizes the need for further studies to verify the efficacy of vaccines in the local context.

Title: The protoxin Cry1Ac of Bacillus thuringiensis improves the protection conferred by intranasal immunization with Brucella abortus RB51 in a mouse model.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Intranasal challenge with virulent strain B. abortus 2308
Vaccine Efficacy: Increased immunoprotection, decreased splenic bacterial load
Immune Response: Increased production of TNF-α and IFN-γ; significant IgG2a response; greater in vivo cytotoxic activity; proliferation of cytotoxic TCD8+ cells
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the co-administration of the Cry1Ac protein as an adjuvant with the RB51 vaccine strain of Brucella abortus to enhance protection against brucellosis.

Title: Brucella abortus S19 and RB51 vaccine immunogenicity test: Evaluation of three mice (BALB/c, Swiss and CD-1) and two challenge strains (544 and 2308).
Vaccine Efficacy: S19 was more protective than RB51 in Swiss mice; both vaccines showed lower counts in vaccinated groups compared to non-vaccinated.
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the immunogenicity of B. abortus vaccines S19 and RB51 using different mouse strains and challenge strains.

Title: Mutation of purD and purF genes further attenuates Brucella abortus strain RB51.
Lab Model or Cell: murine macrophage-like RAW264.7 and HeLa cells
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Transposon mutagenesis, intracellular survival assessment, clearance in mice
Vaccine Efficacy: Protected mice against a challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 544
Vaccine Introduction: The study focuses on the attenuation of the Brucella abortus RB51 vaccine strain through mutations in purD and purF genes.

Title: Economic analysis of vaccination to control bovine brucellosis in the States of Sao Paulo and Mato Grosso, Brazil.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the economic analysis of the S19 vaccine for controlling bovine brucellosis in Brazil.

Title: Immunization with Brucella VirB proteins reduces organ colonization in mice through a Th1-type immune response and elicits a similar immune response in dogs.
Vaccine Formulation: Three subcutaneous doses in QuilA adjuvant
Lab Model or Cell: Mice, Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from dogs
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Intraperitoneal challenge with live Brucella abortus, in vitro stimulation with VirB proteins
Vaccine Efficacy: Significant reduction in spleen load of bacteria in mice; positive delayed-type hypersensitivity in dogs
Immune Response: Th1-type immune response, significant production of IFN-γ
Vaccine Introduction: The study assesses the immune response against VirB proteins from Brucella spp. and their potential to protect against infection in mice and dogs.

Title: Sepracell-MN for mononuclear cell separation from cattle: effect on mitogen-and antigen-induced lymphocyte blastogenesis.
Vaccine Efficacy: FH-separated MNC had greater LBT responses for vaccinated calves compared to nonvaccinates
Immune Response: Greater responses observed in vaccinated steers compared to nonvaccinated steers
Vaccine Introduction: The study compares the immune response of MNC from vaccinated and nonvaccinated steers using Brucella abortus antigens.

Title: Improved serodiagnosis of bovine brucellosis by novel synthetic oligosaccharide antigens representing the capping m epitope elements of Brucella O-polysaccharide.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the potential for synthetic oligosaccharide conjugates to serve as surrogates for naturally derived antigens, which may have implications for the design of brucellosis vaccines and diagnostics.

Title: Outbreak investigation and control case report of brucellosis: experience from livestock research centre, Mpwapwa, Tanzania.
Vaccine Introduction: The study mentions the use of the S19 vaccine as part of control measures for brucellosis in cattle.

Title: Brucella suis vaccine strain S2-infected immortalized caprine endometrial epithelial cell lines induce non-apoptotic ER-stress.
Lab Model or Cell: Immortalized caprine endometrial epithelial cell line (hTERT-EECs)
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Infection and replication studies in vitro
Vaccine Introduction: The study describes the infection and replication of Brucella suis vaccine strain S2 in caprine endometrial epithelial cells and the cellular responses induced.

Title: Immune responses of bison and efficacy after booster vaccination with Brucella abortus strain RB51.
Vaccine Formulation: 10(10) CFU of Brucella abortus strain RB51
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Intraconjunctival challenge with B. abortus strain 2308
Vaccine Efficacy: Reduced incidence of infection in fetal and maternal tissues; lower colonization of Brucella organisms
Immune Response: Increased antibody responses, greater IFN-γ and IL-1β production
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the efficacy of Brucella abortus strain RB51 in bison, including the effects of a booster vaccination.

Title: Full-length cDNA cloning, molecular characterization and differential expression analysis of peroxiredoxin 6 from Ovis aries.
Immune Response: Involvement in host immune responses against Brucella infection
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the S2 vaccine strain of brucellosis in relation to its effects on Prdx6 expression in sheep.

Title: Isolation and Identification of Brucella melitensis Biovar 3 from Vaccinated Small Ruminants: A Public Health Threat in Kosovo.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the Rev 1 vaccine strain used for the vaccination of farm animals.

Title: Vaccination with recombinant L7/L12-truncated Omp31 protein induces protection against Brucella infection in BALB/c mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: evaluation of humoral and cellular immune responses
Vaccine Efficacy: significant protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus challenge
Immune Response: strong specific IgG response, significant IFN-γ/IL2 production, T-cell proliferation, Th1 oriented response
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates a fusion protein designed based on the Truncated form of Omp31 and L7-L12 antigens for potential use as a subunit vaccine against Brucella pathogens.

Title: Mutant Brucella abortus membrane fusogenic protein induces protection against challenge infection in mice.
Vaccine Efficacy: induced greater protection than vaccine RB51 and similar protection to vaccine S19
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated the role of Brucella membrane fusogenic protein (Mfp) and outer membrane protein 19 (Omp19) in bacterial pathogenesis and their potential as live vaccine candidates.

Title: Immunogenicity and protective effect of recombinant Brucella abortus Ndk (rNdk) against a virulent strain B. abortus 544 infection in BALB/c mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: evaluation of protective effect against B. abortus infection
Vaccine Efficacy: significantly lower bacterial burden in spleen compared to MBP-immunized mice
Immune Response: induced vigorous IgG production, predominantly cell-mediated immune responses
Vaccine Introduction: rNdk might be a useful candidate for subunit vaccine for brucellosis in animals.

Title: Comparison of Brucella canis genomes isolated from different countries shows multiple variable regions.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the potential use of the genome for vaccine search to reduce the health impact of Brucella canis infection in dogs and humans.

Title: Preparation and Evaluation of a New Lipopolysaccharide-based Conjugate as a Vaccine Candidate for Brucellosis.
Vaccine Formulation: LPS conjugated to Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B outer membrane vesicle (OMV)
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Measurement of anti-LPS IgG in serum after subcutaneous injections
Vaccine Efficacy: Higher titers of IgG compared to LPS and LPS + OMV
Immune Response: Increased IgG titer of ∼5-fold and ∼1.3-fold higher than LPS and LPS + OMV, respectively
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates a new LPS-OMV conjugate as a potential vaccine candidate for brucellosis.

Title: Development of a dual vaccine for prevention of Brucella abortus infection and Escherichia coli O157:H7 intestinal colonization.
Vaccine Efficacy: Induced protective immune response against B. abortus infection
Vaccine Introduction: A bivalent vaccine has been developed that has the potential for preventing the transmission from cattle to humans of Brucella abortus and Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC).

Title: Immunoproteomic identification of immunodominant antigens independent of the time of infection in Brucella abortus 2308-challenged cattle.
Vaccine Introduction: The study examined novel immunogenic proteins that can be used to detect Brucella abortus infection or as an effective subcellular vaccine.

Title: Intermediate rough Brucella abortus S19Δper mutant is DIVA enable, safe to pregnant guinea pigs and confers protection to mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immunization and protection studies in mice and pregnant guinea pigs
Vaccine Efficacy: Conferred protection similar to S19 vaccine
Immune Response: Strong immune response with higher levels of IFN-γ, IgG2a, Th1 cell mediated immunity
Vaccine Introduction: The study describes a modified B. abortus S19 strain, named S19Δper, which exhibits an intermediate rough phenotype and improved safety and immunogenicity properties compared to the S19 vaccine strain.

Title: Immunogenic response to a recombinant pseudorabies virus carrying bp26 gene of Brucella melitensis in mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: one-step growth curve assay, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, serum neutralization test
Vaccine Efficacy: induced high titer of humoral antibodies, high level of Brucella-specific lymphocyte proliferation response, production of interferon gamma
Vaccine Introduction: Live attenuated vaccines are utilized for prophylaxis of brucellosis; however, they retain residual virulence to human and/or animals, as well as interfere with diagnosis.

Title: Cervical Lymph Nodes as a Selective Niche for Brucella during Oral Infections.
Immune Response: locally restricted inflammatory reaction with increased expression levels of interferon γ, interleukin (IL)-6, IL-12, granzyme B and delayed induction of Nos2
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Recombinant L7/L12 protein entrapping PLGA (poly lactide-co-glycolide) micro particles protect BALB/c mice against the virulent B. abortus 544 infection.
Extracted Vaccine Name: rL7/L12 protein encapsulated in PLGA microparticles
Vaccine Efficacy: IgG antibody titre reached a maxima of 2.2×10(5); clearance of splenic bacteria up to 1.69 log units
Immune Response: Mixed IgG isotype profile (IgG1/IgG2a), high levels of IFN-γ (815±55pg/ml)
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates a safe and effective subunit vaccine for Brucella abortus using rL7/L12 protein encapsulated in PLGA microparticles.

Title: Brucella melitensis Biovar 1 and Brucella abortus S19 Vaccine Strain Infections in Milkers Working at Cattle Farms in the Khartoum Area, Sudan.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the isolation of the B. abortus S19 vaccine strain from a human, highlighting the importance of vaccination for controlling bovine brucellosis and the potential for transmission to humans.

Title: A Brucella melitensis M5-90 wboA deletion strain is attenuated and enhances vaccine efficacy.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Assessment of virulence and protective efficiency, immune response evaluation
Vaccine Efficacy: Induced protective immunity comparable to parental strain M5-90
Immune Response: Elicited anti-Brucella-specific IgG response, secretion of IFN-γ and IL-2
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the wboA mutant derived from Brucella melitensis vaccine strain M5-90 and its potential as an attenuated live vaccine candidate against virulent B. melitensis 16M infection.

Title: Protection Provided by an Encapsulated Live Attenuated ΔabcBA Strain of Brucella ovis against Experimental Challenge in a Murine Model.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Experimental challenge with wild-type B. ovis
Vaccine Efficacy: Mild protection, significantly smaller numbers of wild-type B. ovis CFU in livers
Immune Response: Markedly prevented lesions in the spleens and livers
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the Brucella ovis ΔabcBA strain as a vaccine candidate.

Title: Subcutaneous immunization with a novel immunogenic candidate (urease) confers protection against Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis infections.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: immune response and protection elicited by vaccination
Vaccine Efficacy: higher degree of protection with SC vaccination compared to IP vaccination
Immune Response: mixed Th1-Th2 immune responses with high titers of specific IgG1 and IgG2a
Vaccine Introduction: The study examines the use of recombinant Brucella urease as a subunit vaccine candidate against brucellosis.

Title: Improved immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a divalent DNA vaccine encoding Brucella L7/L12-truncated Omp31 fusion protein by a DNA priming and protein boosting regimen.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Comparison of immunogenicity and protective efficacy
Vaccine Efficacy: Improved protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus
Immune Response: Higher IgG1 and IgG2a titers; increased IFN-γ production
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates a divalent DNA vaccine targeting Brucella pathogens, specifically focusing on the L7/L12 and Omp31 antigens.

Title: Evaluation of the combined use of the recombinant Brucella abortus Omp10, Omp19 and Omp28 proteins for the clinical diagnosis of bovine brucellosis.
Extracted Vaccine Name: recombinant Brucella abortus Omp10, Omp19 and Omp28 proteins
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the potential of combined recombinant Brucella outer membrane proteins for serodiagnosis and future vaccine production.

Title: Immune reactivity of sera obtained from brucellosis patients and vaccinated-rabbits to a fusion protein from Brucella melitensis.
Immune Response: antibodies detected in vaccinated rabbits and infected patients
Vaccine Introduction: The study focuses on a chimeric protein as a potential subunit vaccine candidate against Brucella melitensis.

Title: Immune responses and protection induced by Brucella suis S2 bacterial ghosts in mice.
Immune Response: Induced pathogen-specific serum IgG, CD3(+) and CD4(+) T cell responses, secretion of gamma interferon and interleukin-4
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the immunogenicity of Brucella suis bacterial ghosts as a vaccine candidate.

Title: Brucella spp. Lumazine Synthase Induces a TLR4-Mediated Protective Response against B16 Melanoma in Mice.
Vaccine Efficacy: Significant inhibition of tumor growth; 50% of mice did not develop visible tumors
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the immunogenicity of Brucella Lumazine Synthase (BLS) as a preventive vaccine against melanoma.

Title: Comparative genomic analysis of Brucella abortus vaccine strain 104M reveals a set of candidate genes associated with its virulence attenuation.
Vaccine Introduction: The Brucella abortus strain 104M has been used as a vaccine strain in humans against brucellosis for 6 decades in China.

Title: An influenza viral vector Brucella abortus vaccine induces good cross-protection against Brucella melitensis infection in pregnant heifers.
Gene or Protein Antigen: Brucella ribosomal proteins L7/L12 or Omp16
Vaccine Formulation: Influenza viral vector with Montanide Gel01 adjuvant
Vaccine Efficacy: 100% protection against abortion; 90-100% cross-protection against B. melitensis
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses a novel influenza viral vector B. abortus vaccine that provides cross-protection against B. melitensis.

Title: Immunization of BALB/c mice with Brucella abortus 2308ΔwbkA confers protection against wild-type infection.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Evaluation of virulence and protective immunity
Vaccine Efficacy: Induced high protective immunity in mice
Immune Response: Elicited anti-Brucella-specific immunoglobulin G response and secretion of gamma interferon
Vaccine Introduction: The study constructed the Brucella abortus 2308 wbkA mutant (2308ΔwbkA) and evaluated its potential as a vaccine against brucellosis.

Title: Cloning, molecular analysis and epitopics prediction of a new chaperone GroEL Brucella melitensis antigen.
Immune Response: May stimulate cell-mediated and humoral immunity
Vaccine Introduction: The study focuses on the GroEL antigen of Brucella melitensis, which is a major antigen that stimulates the immune system.

Title: Prediction of T cell epitopes of Brucella abortus and evaluation of their protective role in mice.
Gene or Protein Antigen: MHC-I and MHC-II restricted T cell epitopes
Vaccine Efficacy: Significant protection compared to PBS control
Immune Response: Higher splenocyte proliferation and IFN-γ generation
Vaccine Introduction: The study identifies T cell epitopes of Brucella abortus and evaluates their protective role in mice, supporting the feasibility of peptide-based vaccines for brucellosis.

Title: A diagnostic protocol to identify water buffaloes (Bubalus bubalis) vaccinated with Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine.
Immune Response: 56% developed RB51 antigen-specific CFT antibodies; 82% positive to RB51 brucellin skin test
Vaccine Introduction: The use of live vaccine strain RB51 for vaccination of domestic water buffaloes at risk of infection with Brucella abortus is permitted under strict veterinary control.

Title: Community Perceptions on Integrating Animal Vaccination and Health Education by Veterinary and Public Health Workers in the Prevention of Brucellosis among Pastoral Communities of South Western Uganda.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the importance of mass animal vaccination against brucellosis and the need for community education on the disease.

Title: Protective immune-response of aluminium hydroxide gel adjuvanted phage lysate of Brucella abortus S19 in mice against direct virulent challenge with B. abortus 544.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Phage lysate of Brucella abortus S19
Vaccine Formulation: Aluminium hydroxide gel adjuvanted phage lysate
Immune Response: Induced both humoral and cell-mediated immune responses in a dose dependent manner
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the prophylactic efficacies of phage lysate of Brucella abortus S19, comparing it with standard S19 vaccine.

Title: Overexpression of Brucella putative glycosyltransferase WbkA in B. abortus RB51 leads to production of exopolysaccharide.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Overexpression of wbkA gene in strain RB51
Vaccine Efficacy: Induces protective immunity against virulent B. abortus challenge
Vaccine Introduction: B. abortus strain RB51 is a stable rough attenuated mutant which is used as a licensed live vaccine for bovine brucellosis.

Title: Different resistance patterns of reference and field strains of Brucella abortus.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Growth inhibition on media with different inhibitor agents
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the growth of B. abortus reference strains and field isolates, including vaccine strains S19 and RB51, on media with various inhibitors.

Title: Epidemiological Modeling of Bovine Brucellosis in India.
Vaccine Efficacy: One-time vaccination lowered prevalence initially but increased with influx of new susceptible births.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses mass vaccination as a prevention strategy for bovine brucellosis.

Title: Prevalence and spatial distribution of bovine brucellosis in San Luis and La Pampa, Argentina.
Vaccine Introduction: Vaccination with Brucella abortus strain 19 is compulsory for 3-to-8 month-old heifers.

Title: Encapsulated Brucella ovis Lacking a Putative ATP-Binding Cassette Transporter (ΔabcBA) Protects against Wild Type Brucella ovis in Rams.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Experimental challenge with wild type B. ovis
Vaccine Efficacy: Prevented infection and clinical changes induced by wild type B. ovis
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the protection induced by the vaccine candidate B. ovis ΔabcBA against wild type B. ovis in rams.

Title: Immune Response of Calves Vaccinated with Brucella abortus S19 or RB51 and Revaccinated with RB51.
Immune Response: Strong and complex Th1 immune response; higher persistency of IFN-ɣ and CD4+ memory cells compared to RB51
Vaccine Introduction: The study compares immune responses induced by Brucella abortus S19 and RB51 in calves.

Title: Booster vaccination with safe, modified, live-attenuated mutants of Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine confers protective immunity against virulent strains of B. abortus and Brucella canis in BALB/c mice.
Vaccine Efficacy: significant levels of protection against virulent strains
Immune Response: mixed but T-helper-1-biased humoral and cellular immune response
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates modified live-attenuated mutants of the RB51 vaccine to enhance safety and efficacy against brucellosis.

Title: Simultaneous immunization of mice with Omp31 and TF provides protection against Brucella melitensis infection.
Vaccine Efficacy: provided protection against B. melitensis infection comparable to that of vaccine strain Rev.1
Immune Response: exhibited strong antigen-specific recall proliferative response and expressed high amounts of IFN-γ, IL-12, IL-10 and IL-6
Vaccine Introduction: Subunit vaccines consisting of rOmp31 and rTF have emerged as safe and efficacious alternatives to live attenuated Brucella strains.

Title: Human Brucellosis Trends: Re-emergence and Prospects for Control Using a One Health Approach in Azerbaijan (1983-2009).
Vaccine Efficacy: Highlighted improving prospects for human brucellosis control
Vaccine Introduction: The study mentions the vaccination of >10 million small ruminants with Rev1.

Title: Ontology-based representation and analysis of host-Brucella interactions.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the interactions of virulent Brucella strains and live attenuated Brucella vaccine strains, specifically mentioning the B. abortus vaccine strain RB51.

Title: Survey of Omp19 immunogenicity against Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis: influence of nanoparticulation versus traditional immunization.
Vaccine Efficacy: high protection level against B. melitensis and B. abortus
Immune Response: Th1 and Th2 immune responses (Omp19-IFA), mixed Th1/Th17 immune response (TMC/Omp19)
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the immunogenicity of Omp19 as a subunit vaccine candidate against brucellosis, comparing traditional and nanoparticulate formulations.

Title: PLGA (85:15) nanoparticle based delivery of rL7/L12 ribosomal protein in mice protects against Brucella abortus 544 infection: A promising alternate to traditional adjuvants.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Enumeration of splenic CFU after infection
Vaccine Efficacy: significant reduction in log CFU of splenic bacteria in vaccinated mice
Immune Response: elicited high IgG antibody titers and Th1 cytokines, mixed Th1/Th2 response
Vaccine Introduction: The study explores the immunogenic potential of PLGA nanoparticles delivering rL7/L12 protein, an immunodominant antigen of Brucella, highlighting its adjuvant properties and efficacy in eliciting immune responses against Brucella abortus infection.

Title: A bacterial protease inhibitor protects antigens delivered in oral vaccines from digestion while triggering specific mucosal immune responses.
Vaccine Efficacy: Induces mucosal protection and reduces parasite loads
Immune Response: Enhances Ag-specific immune responses, antibodies, Th1, Th17, and CD8(+) T cells
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses U-Omp19 as a bacterial protease inhibitor from Brucella spp. that enhances the efficacy of oral vaccines.

Title: Brucellosis outbreak in a rural endemic region of Mexico - a comprehensive investigation.
Vaccine Introduction: The results of molecular typing did not show any Brucella vaccine strains.

Title: Structural, Functional, and Immunogenic Insights on Cu,Zn Superoxide Dismutase Pathogenic Virulence Factors from Neisseria meningitidis and Brucella abortus.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Passive immunization with an antibody directed at BaSOD
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the role of Cu,Zn superoxide dismutase from Brucella abortus as a potential target for vaccine development against brucellosis.

Title: Immunization of Mice with Recombinant Brucella abortus Organic Hydroperoxide Resistance (Ohr) Protein Protects Against a Virulent Brucella abortus 544 Infection.
Vaccine Formulation: Purified recombinant protein treated with adjuvant
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immunization and protective immune response analysis
Vaccine Efficacy: Induced significant protection against virulent B. abortus infection
Immune Response: Induced both humoral (IgG1 and IgG2a) and cell-mediated immunity (high IFN-γ and proinflammatory cytokines)
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of the recombinant Ohr protein as a potential vaccine candidate for animal brucellosis.

Title: A novel lumazine synthase molecule from Brucella significantly promotes the immune-stimulation effects of antigenic protein.
Vaccine Introduction: The intact Brucella suis outer membrane protein 31 (omp31) gene was cloned and examined as a subunit vaccine candidate. The intact Brucella lumazine synthase (bls) gene was also cloned and expressed to study its function.

Title: Draft Genome Sequence of the Intermediate Rough Vaccine Strain Brucella abortus S19Δper Mutant.
Vaccine Introduction: The study reports the genome sequence of the intermediate rough vaccine strain mutant, Brucella abortus S19Δper.

Title: Novel Vaccine Candidates against Brucella melitensis Identified through Reverse Vaccinology Approach.
Gene or Protein Antigen: LPS-assembly protein LptD, polysaccharide export protein, cell surface protein, heme transporter BhuA, flagellin FliC, 7-alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, immunoglobulin-binding protein EIBE, hemagglutinin
Vaccine Introduction: The study identifies eight proteins as potential vaccine candidates against B. melitensis using a reverse vaccinology approach.

Title: Serological diagnostic potential of recombinant outer membrane proteins (rOMPs) from Brucella melitensis in mouse model using indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: antibody response investigation using RBPT and rOMPs I-ELISA
Vaccine Introduction: The study also discusses recombinant outer membrane proteins (rOMP25, rOMP28, rOMP31) as diagnostic antigens for serological tests.

Title: Comparative analyses of proteins extracted by hot saline or released spontaneously into outer membrane blebs from field strains of Brucella ovis and Brucella melitensis.
Gene or Protein Antigen: proteins of 43 kDa, group A (25.5 to 32.0 kDa), group B (21.5 to 22.5 kDa), group C (18.0 to 19.5 kDa), group D (13.0 to 15.5 kDa)
Immune Response: antibody responses to rough lipopolysaccharide and proteins in HS extracts
Vaccine Introduction: The study identifies proteins from Brucella ovis that may serve as components of a subcellular vaccine for ovine brucellosis.

Title: Immunization with individual proteins of the Lrp/AsnC family induces protection against Brucella melitensis 16M challenges in mice.
Gene or Protein Antigen: BMEI0357 and other Lrp/AsnC family proteins
Vaccine Formulation: Recombinant proteins expressed in Escherichia coli
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Protective efficacy evaluation in mice challenged with Brucella melitensis 16M
Vaccine Efficacy: Induced protective immune response against Brucella melitensis 16M
Immune Response: Antibodies against Lrp/AsnC proteins detected in immunized mice
Vaccine Introduction: The study identifies six proteins of the Lrp/AsnC family as potential subunit vaccines for brucellosis prevention.

Title: Brucella discriminates between mouse dendritic cell subsets upon in vitro infection.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses Brucella's interaction with dendritic cell subsets and suggests potential for using dendritic cells as cellular vaccines to enhance immune response against pathogens.

Title: [Genetic stability of the HA, NA, and NS genes of the recombinant vector virus Flu-NS1-124-Omp16 (H5N1) expressing the brucellar gene].
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses a recombinant strain of the influenza virus that expresses the brucellar Omp16 gene for the purpose of developing a vector anti-brucellosis vaccine.

Title: Brucella abortusΔcydCΔcydD and ΔcydCΔpurD double-mutants are highly attenuated and confer long-term protective immunity against virulent Brucella abortus.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: In vivo and in vitro assays
Vaccine Efficacy: Provided significantly better protection than commercial B. abortus strain RB51 vaccine
Immune Response: Induced humoral and cell-mediated immune responses
Vaccine Introduction: The study focuses on double deletion mutants of Brucella abortus that are highly attenuated and confer long-term protective immunity against virulent Brucella abortus.

Title: Innocuity and immune response to Brucella melitensis Rev.1 vaccine in camels (Camelus dromedarius).
Vaccine Efficacy: Induces seroconversion in camels; no isolation of Brucella melitensis from milk
Immune Response: Antibody response observed starting at week 2, remained positive until week 16
Vaccine Introduction: Study evaluates the Rev.1 vaccine in camels and assesses shedding of the vaccine strain in milk.

Title: Brucella melitensis 16MΔTcfSR as a potential live vaccine allows for the differentiation between natural and vaccinated infection.
Vaccine Efficacy: induced a high level of protective immunity
Immune Response: elicited an anti-Brucella-specific IgG response and induced the secretion of interferon-γ
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the drawbacks of existing live attenuated vaccines for brucellosis and presents the B. melitensis 16MΔTcfSR mutant as a safer and more effective alternative.

Title: Brucella suis strain 2 vaccine is safe and protective against heterologous Brucella spp. infections.
Target Vaccine Recipient or Host: goats, sheep, cattle, swine, BALB/c mice
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: determination of bacteria persistence in spleen, serum antibody response, cellular immune response, protection against heterologous virulent challenge

Title: Non-specific stimulation of human B lymphocytes by a Brucella fraction.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses a lipid A-free fraction from Brucella melitensis that acts as a non-specific mitogen and polyclonal B-cell activator.

Title: Immunomodulation of primary antitoxic-type immunity with inactivated Brucella suspensions.
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Serological response of cattle, sheep and goats in Kenya vaccinated with killed Brucella melitensis strain H38 adjuvant vaccine.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Serum (tube) agglutination, complement fixation, and Rose Bengal plate tests
Immune Response: Induced by a single dose of the vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: An evaluation of the anamnestic test for brucellosis in cattle of the northern pastoral area.
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the anamnestic test for brucellosis using Brucella abortus 45/20 vaccine in cattle.

Title: Immune response to porin in cattle immunized with whole cell, outer membrane, and outer membrane protein antigens of Brucella abortus combined with trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide adjuvants.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Nonliving vaccines derived from Brucella abortus rough strain 45/20
Vaccine Formulation: Outer membrane proteins with trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Factorial experiment to test immune response
Vaccine Efficacy: Antibody responses improved with increased oil quantity; responses sustained for over 3 months
Immune Response: Delayed-type hypersensitivity and blastogenesis responses exceeded those after natural or experimental infections
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates immune responses to nonliving vaccines derived from Brucella abortus in cattle, focusing on the effects of different antigens and adjuvants.

Title: Comparison of radioimmunoassay with the complement fixation test and the indirect haemolysis test in the field diagnosis of bovine brucellosis.
Vaccine Introduction: Vaccination of heifer calves with Brucella abortus strain 19 was compulsory.

Title: Vaccination of calves against brucellosis
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Serological response of calfhood strain 19 vaccinated cows to oral dosing with Brucella abortus strain 19.
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the serological response of cows vaccinated with Brucella abortus strain 19.

Title: Comparison of an agar-gel immunodiffusion test with other serological methods for differentiating Brucella infected from vaccinated cattle.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Serological tests for detection of antibodies
Vaccine Introduction: The study involved cattle vaccinated with Brucella abortus strain 19 and compared serological tests for detecting antibodies.

Title: Effect of oxytetracycline administration on antibody response to Brucella abortus vaccination in calves.
Vaccine Efficacy: reduced percentage of animals with detectable humoral antibodies
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the effect of oxytetracycline on the antibody response to Brucella abortus vaccination in calves, specifically focusing on strain 19.

Title: Application of indomethacin as a potentiator of lymphocyte blastogenesis in Brucella abortus exposed cattle.
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the effects of indomethacin on lymphocyte responses in cattle vaccinated with strain 19 and exposed to Brucella abortus.

Title: The serological response of adult cattle to vaccination with reduced dose Brucella abortus S19, a trial under Zambian conditions.
Vaccine Efficacy: All cattle were negative to the serological tests twelve months after vaccination
Vaccine Introduction: The study supports the use of reduced dose S19 under local conditions in Zambia.

Title: Immune depression in bovine trypanosomiasis: effects of acute and chronic Trypanosoma congolense and chronic Trypanosoma vivax infections on antibody response to Brucella abortus vaccine.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Antibody response measurement during Trypanosoma infections
Vaccine Efficacy: Antibody responses were profoundly depressed during acute and chronic infections
Immune Response: IgG1 and IgG2 sub-classes were depressed by 80% in acute and chronic T. congolense infections; IgM was depressed by 90% in acute and 50% in chronic infections
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the effects of Trypanosoma infections on the immune response to the Brucella abortus vaccine.

Title: Immune serum-mediated effects on brucellosis evolution in mice.
Extracted Vaccine Name: protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan Brucella fraction
Immune Response: induced both early and late effects on infection
Vaccine Introduction: Other immune sera studied include Brucella lipopolysaccharide and polysaccharide cross-reacting Yersinia immune sera.

Title: The anamnestic response to Brucella abortus-infected and vaccinated cattle.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus strain 19 (S19) and B. abortus 45/20 (S45/20)
Vaccine Efficacy: 75% sensitivity and 100% specificity in serologically negative cattle
Immune Response: Positive anamnestic response in vaccinated cattle
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the anamnestic response in cattle vaccinated with Brucella abortus strains S19 and S45/20.

Title: Vaccine and serum-mediated protection against brucella infection of mouse placenta.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: brucella enumeration in placentas and dams' spleens
Vaccine Efficacy: decreased frequency of placental colonization and number of brucella per infected placenta and per spleen
Immune Response: immunity transferred persisted for at least 3 days
Vaccine Introduction: The study also mentions protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan (PG) fractions and B19 attenuated living vaccines as protective against brucella infection.

Title: Protection by oral administration of brucella abortus strain 19 against an oral challenge exposure with a pathogenic strain of Brucella.
Vaccine Efficacy: None of the vaccinates aborted; 14 control heifers were culture positive
Immune Response: Titers after oral vaccination persisted for less than 82 days
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the efficacy of oral vaccination with Brucella abortus strain 19 against a pathogenic strain of Brucella.

Title: Phase I study of immunotherapy by live Brucella abortus (strain 19 BA) in cancer patients.
Immune Response: increase of polymorphonuclear cells and lymphocytes
Vaccine Introduction: The study involved a live Brucella abortus vaccine administered to cancer patients with negative responses against Brucella antigens.

Title: [Comparative study of the safety, reactogenicity and antigenic activity of chemical and live brucellosis vaccines in a controlled epidemiological trial].
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Comparative study of safety, reactogenicity, and antigenic activity
Vaccine Efficacy: No statistically significant differences in antibody titers compared to live vaccine
Immune Response: Antigenic and immunogenic potency comparable to live vaccine; lower sensitizing activity than live vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: Live brucellosis vaccine was also studied for comparison.

Title: Assessment of an intradermal test for the detection of bovine brucellosis.
Vaccine Efficacy: 40 of the remaining 46 gave a positive response to the intradermal test at 48 hours
Vaccine Introduction: Also studied Brucella abortus 45/20 (S45/20) as a vaccine.

Title: Comparison of sodium dodecyl sulfate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis profiles and antigenic relatedness among outer membrane proteins of 49 Brucella abortus strains.
Vaccine Introduction: The study suggests that outer membrane proteins from a representative strain of B. abortus may be used in a vaccine for species-wide immunization.

Title: An hemolysis-in-gel test for bovine brucellosis.
Immune Response: HIGT reactions appeared later than reactions to other tests, persisted as long as 565 days
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluated the hemolysis-in-gel test for detecting antibodies against Brucella abortus in vaccinated heifers.

Title: Biochemical and biological properties of soluble protein preparations from Brucella abortus.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Soluble protein preparations from Brucella abortus
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immunization studies, ELISA for antibody detection
Vaccine Efficacy: Decreased humoral antibody levels without loss of protective activity
Immune Response: Antigenic and immunogenic in multiple animal models
Vaccine Introduction: Other soluble protein antigen preparations have also been evaluated and compared with strain 19 proteins for immunogenic properties and for use as an ELISA reagent.

Title: Evaluation of a radial immunodiffusion test for diagnosing brucellosis in sheep and its possible value for differentiating infected from Brucella melitensis REV 1 vaccinated sheep.
Immune Response: Decreased percentage of CF reactors from about 30% to less than 8% between weeks 24 and 52; RID reactors were 1% and 0% at weeks 24 and 52 respectively.
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the serological response of sheep following vaccination with the REV 1 strain of Brucella melitensis.

Title: Human brucellosis vaccine obtained from the phenol-insoluble fraction of Brucella abortus strain B 19. Production, control, standardization.
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: An evaluation of the stability of Brucella abortus strain 19 reduced dosage lyophilized vaccines produced by different methods.
Vaccine Introduction: The study evaluates the stability of Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine produced by different methods, focusing on cell concentration and fill volume.

Title: Brucellosis control in an infected herd by serological testing, removal of reactors, vaccination with reduced dose of strain 19 and improved hygiene.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the use of a reduced dose of strain 19 vaccine in a herd of cattle to control brucellosis.

Title: Characterization of salt-extractable protein antigens from Brucella abortus by crossed immunoelectrophoresis and isoelectricfocusing.
Vaccine Introduction: The study analyzes protein antigens from Brucella abortus strains 19 (vaccine) and 2308 (virulent).

Title: Detection of serum antibody to Brucella abortus in cattle by use of a quantitative fluorometric immunoassay.
Immune Response: Statistically significant difference in mean titers between vaccinates and controls
Vaccine Introduction: The study involved cattle vaccinated with strain 19 and assessed their immune response through serological tests.

Title: Evaluation of the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in the detection of cattle infected with Brucella abortus.
Vaccine Efficacy: High levels of IgG and IgM detected
Immune Response: High levels of IgG and IgM in vaccinated cattle
Vaccine Introduction: Another vaccine studied was B. abortus S45/20, which produced detectable antibody in only a few cattle.

Title: Isolation of Brucella abortus from supramammary lymph nodes of cattle from infected herds vaccinated with low dose strain 19.
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Proposed general method of controlling the activity of brucella vaccines
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Theoretical, practical and statistical basis for a general control method of activity for anti-Brucella vaccines.
Vaccine Introduction: killed whole cells and purified fractions vaccines were also studied.

Title: Immunization of ewes and she-goats against experimental Brucella melitensis infection. A comparison of REV 1 and H 38 vaccines.
Vaccine Introduction: H 38 vaccine is also mentioned.

Title: Protection of rams against epididymitis by a Brucella ovis-vitamin E adjuvant vaccine.
Vaccine Introduction: Other vaccines studied include Freund's incomplete adjuvant and commercial bacterin.

Title: [Brucella vaccination administered via the conjunctiva]
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Vaccination against bovine brucellosis.
Vaccine Efficacy: Immunity comparable to conventional calfhood vaccination
Immune Response: Reduced serological response in most cattle
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates modifications to strain 19 vaccination and alternative methods for effective vaccination against bovine brucellosis.

Title: Control of ovine brucellosis in Najdi sheep in Saudi Arabia.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: serological testing and monitoring of sheep
Vaccine Efficacy: abortions and infertility problems had disappeared; lambing percentage increased from 0.8 to 1.3 lambs per ewe
Immune Response: all young lambs born to vaccinated ewes were found to be serologically negative
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: A note on adult sheep vaccination with reduced dose of Brucella melitensis Rev 1.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Serological response tests (rose bengal, complement fixation, radial immunodiffusion)
Vaccine Efficacy: Little or no effect on the normal development of pregnancy
Vaccine Introduction: The study describes results obtained by vaccinating pregnant ewes with a reduced dose of Brucella melitensis Rev 1.

Title: Histopathology of experimental brucellosis in rams following vaccination with Brucella ovis.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: comparison of lesions in vaccinated vs unvaccinated rams
Immune Response: increased neutrophils, macrophages, and lymphocytes; exacerbated lesions
Vaccine Introduction: The study compares the effects of vaccination with B. ovis bacterin on the histopathology of experimental brucellosis in rams.

Title: Vaccination of cattle with Brucella abortus strain 19 administered by differing routes and doses.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Comparative study of different doses and routes of administration
Vaccine Efficacy: Efficacy found to be influenced little by route of administration
Vaccine Introduction: Study re-examines the use of Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccination in cattle for brucellosis control.

Title: Use of vaccine H 38 in preventing bovine and ovine brucellosis in France
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: A laboratory reference vaccine to titrate immunogenic activity of antibrucella vaccines in mice.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses a reference vaccine prepared from B. melitensis strains H38 to standardize the assessment of immunogenic activity of antibrucella vaccines in mice.

Title: Induction of autoantibodies and circulating immune complexes in mice after injection of Brucella fraction "PI" or inoculation with live Brucella suis.
Vaccine Efficacy: Induction of autoantibodies and circulating immune complexes
Immune Response: Increased levels of anti-ssDNA antibodies, induction of rheumatoid factor, appearance of circulating immune complexes
Vaccine Introduction: Live Brucella suis was also studied but with weaker effects compared to the Brucella fraction "PI".

Title: Effect of cyclophosphamide on specific IgM and IgG responses and recovery during the various stages of persistent immunization in the Brucella-rabbit model.
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the effects of cyclophosphamide on the immune response in rabbits immunized with Brucella abortus.

Title: Serological response of sheep to Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine.
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Vaccination of cattle against brucellosis using either a reduced dose of strain 19 or one or two doses of 45/20 vaccine.
Vaccine Efficacy: One dose of 45/20 vaccine induced resistance to virulent B. abortus approximately equal to that given by the reduced dose of strain 19.
Immune Response: One dose of 45/20 vaccine stimulated transient serological positivity in 2 of 28 heifers; reduced dose of strain 19 gave rise to persistent titres in 2 of 14 vaccinated heifers.
Vaccine Introduction: The study compares the efficacy of one and two doses of B. abortus 45/20 vaccine and a reduced dose of strain 19 vaccine in cattle against brucellosis.

Title: Comparison of different antigenic preparations for the detection of ovine serum antibodies against Brucella ovis by ELISA.
Immune Response: High level of antibody activity detected in vaccinated rams
Vaccine Introduction: The study compares different antigenic preparations for detecting antibodies against Brucella ovis in rams, including those vaccinated intramuscularly.

Title: Reversion of attenuated vaccine "Brucellovac" after passage in laboratory animals irradiated with gamma rays
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: passage in laboratory animals irradiated with gamma rays
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Brucella abortus (strain 19) vaccine: (a) determination of the minimum protective dose in cattle; (b) the effect of vaccinating calves previously inoculated with anti-Brucella abortus serum.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Determination of minimum protective dose and effect of prior serum inoculation
Vaccine Introduction: The study focuses on the Brucella abortus (strain 19) vaccine and its protective dose in cattle.

Title: Comparison of the complement fixation test and the indirect hemolysis test for cattle vaccinated and infected with Brucella abortus.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Complement fixation test (CFT) and indirect hemolysis test (IHLT)
Vaccine Introduction: The study involved cattle vaccinated with either B. abortus 19 or B. abortus 45/20.

Title: Allergenic activity and biochemical analysis of three soluble antigen preparations from Brucella abortus strain 45/20.
Vaccine Introduction: Three Brucella abortus strain 45/20 antigen preparations were compared for allergenic potential.

Title: [Immune response of guinea pigs to combined action of brucella vaccine and homologous lysed antigen].
Extracted Vaccine Name: Brucella vaccine prepared from Br. abortus 82
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: synergetic effect on antibacterial immunity index
Vaccine Efficacy: increased number of immune animals 1.5-2 times
Vaccine Introduction: study of the combined action of a live brucellosis vaccine and a lyzed Brucella component.

Title: [Trials of the use of live vaccines against brucellosis and listeriosis in farm animals].
Vaccine Efficacy: up to 100 percent in certain contaminated areas
Vaccine Introduction: A live vaccine against brucellosis was developed on the basis of strain Brucella abortus 82.

Title: Colonization of mouse placentas by Brucella abortus inoculated during pregnancy.
Vaccine Efficacy: protected against i.p. challenge with 2 x 10(5) brucella
Vaccine Introduction: The study mentions the use of H.38 B. melitensis killed vaccine in mice immunized 36 days before pregnancy.

Title: Vaccination of pregnant cows with low doses of Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine.
Vaccine Formulation: Reduced doses of Brucella abortus strain 19
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Challenge with virulent strain of B. abortus biotype 1
Vaccine Efficacy: Resistance to challenge was similar in both vaccinated groups and higher than previously demonstrated after conventional calfhood vaccination
Immune Response: Marked reduction in the serological response to vaccination was seen only in Group 2
Vaccine Introduction: Two groups of Jersey cows were vaccinated subcutaneously with reduced doses of Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine early in their second pregnancy.

Title: Immunogenic properties of soluble antigens or whole cells of Brucella abortus strain 45/20 associated with immunoadjuvants. I. Soluble antigens.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Purified protein derivative-live preparation of Brucella abortus strain 45/20
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Intradermal inoculation followed by intramuscular challenge
Vaccine Efficacy: Reduced mean colony counts by 32 to 61%
Vaccine Introduction: Whole cells of strain 45/20 in Freund's complete adjuvant were more effective than purified protein derivative-like preparations.

Title: Effect of Brucella abortus on growth of ovarian granulosa cell carcinoma
Vaccine Efficacy: inhibits growth of granular cell ovarian carcinoma
Immune Response: mediated through peritoneal exudate cells and spleen cells
Vaccine Introduction: killed B. abortus vaccine also demonstrated similar action.

Title: Comparison of muramyl dipeptide, trehalose dimycolate, and dimethyl dioctadecyl ammonium bromide as adjuvants in Brucella abortus 45/20 vaccines.
Adjuvant: trehalose dimycolate, muramyl dipeptide, dimethyl dioctadecyl ammonium bromide
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: comparison of adjuvants in vaccine formulations
Vaccine Efficacy: effective in prevention of brucellosis with TDM in oil emulsion
Vaccine Introduction: The study compares the effectiveness of different adjuvants in enhancing the immunogenicity of killed Brucella abortus 45/20 vaccines.

Title: Failure of a single dose of Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine to protect cattle when given early in calfhood.
Vaccine Efficacy: Not effectively protected when given at 3 to 5 weeks without boost; effective with boost
Immune Response: Slight and transient serological responses in a few animals
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the efficacy of Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine in cattle, particularly focusing on the timing of vaccination and the effect of an intraconjunctival boost.

Title: Immunogenic properties of soluble antigens or whole cells of Brucella abortus strain 45/20 associated with immunoadjuvants. II. Whole cells.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Whole cells of Brucella abortus strain 45/20
Vaccine Efficacy: Reduced mean splenic Brucella by 95.1% (muramyl dipeptide) and 99.3% (trehalose dimycolate)
Vaccine Introduction: Whole cells of Brucella abortus strain 45/20 were tested with adjuvants for immunogenic properties.

Title: Immunoglobulin classes in serum antibody reactions in cattle following vaccination with Brucella abortus strain 19 and killed 45/20 vaccines.
Vaccine Efficacy: increased titres to the smooth antigen
Vaccine Introduction: The study involved vaccination with Brucella abortus strain 19 followed by the B. abortus 45/20 vaccine.

Title: Comparison of B. melitensis Rev. 1 and B. abortus strain 19 as a vaccine against brucellosis in cattle.
Vaccine Introduction: B. abortus strain 19 is also mentioned as a vaccine against brucellosis in cattle.

Title: Immunological characteristics in cattle of allergens derived from smooth Brucella abortus S99.
Vaccine Formulation: Allergen derived from smooth Brucella abortus S99
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Intradermal test for diagnosis of brucellosis
Immune Response: Does not cause production of complement fixing or agglutinating antibodies
Vaccine Introduction: The study describes the development and testing of an allergen for diagnosing brucellosis in cattle.

Title: Serological differentiation between infected and vaccinated cattle by using purified soluble antigens from Brucella abortus in a hemagglutination system.
Vaccine Efficacy: Improved discrimination between infected and vaccinated cattle
Vaccine Introduction: Also mentions Brucella abortus strain 45/20 as a vaccine studied.

Title: Prevalence and persistence of Brucella abortus strain 19 infections and prevalence of other biotypes in vaccinated adult dairy cattle.
Vaccine Efficacy: Shedding rates reported (1.4% conjunctival, 0.83% standard subcutaneous, 0.45% reduced subcutaneous)
Immune Response: Approximately 20% of shedders were seropositive 13-18 months later
Vaccine Introduction: Vaccination methods included conjunctival and subcutaneous routes, with varying efficacy observed.

Title: Ultrastructural localization of characterized antigens of Brucella abortus and distribution among different biotypes.
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates characterized antigens in Brucella abortus, including the vaccine strain 19 extract.

Title: Increased resistance to tumor graft in mice infected by vaccinal strains of Brucella abortus.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Kinetics of proliferation in vivo and effect on murine tumors
Vaccine Efficacy: Favorable results in EL4 lymphoma and Lewis tumor
Vaccine Introduction: Two derivatives, 19BA and B19R, were also studied.

Title: Development of a migration inhibitory factor assay under agarose of bovine mononuclear leukocytes, using an antigen of Brucella abortus.
Vaccine Introduction: The study involved calves previously vaccinated with strain 19 of Brucella abortus.

Title: Effects of killed Brucella abortus strain 45/20 vaccine on reindeer later challenge exposed with Brucella suis type 4.
Vaccine Formulation: killed Brucella abortus strain 45/20 with added adjuvant
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: challenge exposure with Brucella suis type 4
Immune Response: humoral antibodies detected by postvaccination day 14
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the effects of a killed Brucella abortus strain 45/20 vaccine on reindeer challenged with Brucella suis type 4.

Title: The isolation of Brucella abortus biotype I from serologically positive reactors following on S19 adult inoculation of dairy cows.
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the isolation of Brucella abortus biotype I following S19 vaccination in dairy cows.

Title: Characterisation of Brucella abortus strain 19 cultures isolated from vaccinated cattle.
Vaccine Introduction: The study characterizes cultures of Brucella abortus strain 19 isolated from vaccinated cattle, noting the properties and virulence tests of the strain.

Title: Some observations on antigenic properties and immunogenic effects of brucella vaccine PB19.
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: [Brucella keratoconjunctivitis].
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses a case involving the Brucella abortus vaccine and its accidental exposure leading to keratoconjunctivitis in a veterinarian.

Title: Serologic response of pigs to experimental infection with Yersinia enterocolitica serotype O9 and Brucella abortus.
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: The bovine immune response to Brucella abortus IV. Studies with a double immunodiffusion test for antibody against A2.
Vaccine Introduction: The study mentions cattle vaccinated with killed B. melitensis strain H38 and live B. abortus strain 19.

Title: BrucELISA: an enzyme-antibody immunoassay for detection of Brucella abortus antibodies in milk: correlation with the Brucella ring test and with shedding of viable organisms.
Vaccine Introduction: BrucELISA is described for the detection of antibody to Brucella abortus in cow's milk.

Title: Comparison of Brucella abortus (strain 544) variants.
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: The serological response of cattle to vaccines against brucellosis, as measured by the brucellosis radioimmunoassay and other tests.
Vaccine Introduction: Killed B. abortus strain 45/20 adjuvant (K45/20A) vaccine was also studied.

Title: Brucella abortus vaccines: comparison of protection provided by immunopotentiated 45/20 bacterins and live strain 19 vaccine in guinea pigs.
Vaccine Formulation: 300 microgram of Brucella abortus strain 45/20 killed cells in 1% oil emulsion with trehalose dimycolate (TDM), muramyl dipeptide (MDP), or a combination of the 2
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: comparison of protection against splenic infections after challenge exposure
Vaccine Introduction: The study compares the protection provided by immunopotentiated 45/20 bacterins and live strain 19 vaccine.

Title: Persistence of Brucella abortus strain 19 infection in adult cattle vaccinated with reduced doses.
Vaccine Introduction: Study of reduced doses of Brucella abortus strain 19 in cattle.

Title: Effect of antibiotics on the development of immune response in the organism of animals. IV. Rabbit experiments with a Brucella vaccine (B19) and its heat-inactivated variant.
Vaccine Introduction: heat-inactivated variant of Brucella vaccine (B19)

Title: The effect of challenge with virulent Brucella abortus on beef cattle vaccinated as calves or adults with either Brucella abortus strain 19 or 45/20.
Vaccine Efficacy: 15 healthy calves born to 18 vaccinated with S19
Vaccine Introduction: Also studied Brucella abortus strain 45/20 (S45/20).

Title: Leukocyte migration-inhibition responses of nonvaccinated and vaccinated heifers to experimental infection with Brucella abortus.
Vaccine Efficacy: vaccinated heifers had significantly lower responses compared to nonvaccinated heifers
Immune Response: increased leukocyte migration inhibition after exposure to B abortus
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the immune response of vaccinated heifers to Brucella abortus infection compared to nonvaccinated heifers.

Title: Isolation of three Brucella abortus cell-wall antigens protective in murine experimental brucellosis.
Vaccine Formulation: Injected subcutaneously with Freund incomplete adjuvant
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immunity tested by challenge with virulent strain of B. abortus
Vaccine Efficacy: Protective at a level corresponding to killed whole-cells Brucella melitensis H38 reference vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: Three major bands of cell-wall antigens were isolated and tested for protective efficacy in mice.

Title: Levamisole potentiation of antigen specific lymphocyte blastogenic response in Brucella abortus exposed but nonresponsive cattle.
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the effects of levamisole on the immune response of cattle vaccinated with Brucella abortus strain 19.

Title: Effect of temperature and degree of vacuum on the conservation of freeze-dried Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Antibodies to Brucella abortus in sera from Strain 19 vaccinated and non-vaccinated cows as determined by enzyme linked immunosorbent assay and conventional serologic methods.
Vaccine Efficacy: Antibodies detected in more than 93% of culture positive cows
Immune Response: Antibodies detected in 82% of culture negative cows
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Serological response of cattle after vaccination and challenge with Brucella abortus.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Serological evaluation after vaccination and challenge
Immune Response: Titres rose more slowly, declined more rapidly
Vaccine Introduction: Also studied B. abortus 45/20 (S45/20) as a vaccine.

Title: Bovine immunoglobulins and brucellosis. IV. Study by microchromatographic technique of class types of persistent antibodies found in heifers vaccinated 12 to 14 months previously with Brucella abortus strain 19.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Microchromatography technique to study antibody classes
Immune Response: Persistent antibodies were nearly exclusively of IgM type
Vaccine Introduction: The study focuses on heifers vaccinated with Brucella abortus strain 19 and the analysis of their antibody response.

Title: [Cell survival of the Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine during the lyophilization process according to the vehicle used].
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Comparative study of stabilizing media for lyophilization
Vaccine Efficacy: Viable count averages ranging from 50% to 58% for six media
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the stabilization of Brucella abortus strain 19 during lyophilization using various media.

Title: [Determination of the optimal inoculation dose of Brucella chemical vaccine].
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Wright's agglutination test and Huddleson's test
Vaccine Efficacy: Highest antigenic and immunogenic activity observed with a dose of 1 mg
Immune Response: High percentage of seroconversions, highest titers of agglutinins, longest persistence
Vaccine Introduction: The study tested four doses of a brucellosis chemical vaccine, identifying 1 mg as the optimal dose for immunogenic activity.

Title: Course of chronic brucellosis in mice is not improved by administration of a vaccinal antigen
Vaccine Formulation: extracted by boiling sodium dodecylsulfate suspended in oil adjuvant
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: subcutaneous injections and enumeration of brucella in spleen
Immune Response: additional antigenic stimulation unable to improve immune response
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the effects of a B. abortus 19 cell-wall vaccine in a mouse model of chronic brucellosis.

Title: A study of cattle infected with Brucella abortus and which showed aberrant serological reactions.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus strain 19 (S19) and Brucella abortus strain 45/20 (S45/20)
Vaccine Introduction: The study involved two vaccines, S19 and S45/20, used in cattle to assess their response to subsequent infection with B. abortus strain 544.

Title: Comparative efficacy of an experimental S45/20 bacterin and a reduced dose of strain 19 vaccine against bovine brucellosis.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Comparative study with reduced dose of strain 19 vaccine
Vaccine Efficacy: Poor protection observed; 84.2% abortions in S45/20 group
Immune Response: Delayed hypersensitivity in 16 of 21 heifers given S45/20
Vaccine Introduction: Study compares S45/20 bacterin with strain 19 vaccine against bovine brucellosis.

Title: The use of the non-specific immunological factors, conglutinin, immunoconglutinin and heterophile antibody, in the serodiagnosis of bovine brucellosis.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Measurement of immunoconglutinin, conglutinin, and heterophile antibodies
Immune Response: IK titres rose rapidly following vaccination but returned to normal within ten weeks
Vaccine Introduction: The study involved calves vaccinated with Br. abortus Strain 19.

Title: [Comparative cytoenzymatic study of infectious and vaccinal processes in experimental brucellosis].
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: metabolic changes in peripheral blood cells
Vaccine Introduction: The study compares the effects of the vaccinal culture of Br. abortus 19 with the virulent culture of Br. abortus 544.

Title: Mitogenic activity of two Brucella fractions for murine B lymphocytes.
Vaccine Introduction: Two lipid A-free fractions (PI and SF) from Brucella melitensis were studied for their mitogenic activity on murine B lymphocytes.

Title: [Certain indices of cell-mediated immunity among brucellosis patients who were vaccinated and react positively to brucellin].
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: analysis of T-lymphocytes and macrophages in vaccinated patients
Immune Response: presence of T-lymphocytes sensitized to brucellosis antigen
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the immune response in patients vaccinated with a live brucellosis vaccine.

Title: IgE anti-brucella antibodies in the course of human brucellosis and after specific vaccination.

Title: The role of T cell subsets and cytokines in the regulation of intracellular bacterial infection.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Adoptive transfer of transgenic macrophage clones
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the potential for vaccines designed to activate protective T cell subsets against Brucella abortus.

Title: Evaluation of a rough mutant of Brucella melitensis in pregnant goats.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: evaluation of vaccine efficacy in pregnant goats
Vaccine Efficacy: partial protection against infection and abortion
Immune Response: does not induce anti-O chain antibodies
Vaccine Introduction: rough derivative of B melitensis strain 16M, does not induce abortion in pregnant goats at doses leading to abortions with virulent strain 16M.

Title: Value of different serological tests in the diagnosis of bovine brucellosis in the Amazonian region.
Vaccine Introduction: The study involved the vaccination of heifer calves with the B19 vaccine and evaluated the serological response using various tests.

Title: Field study of vaccination of cattle with Brucella abortus strains RB51 and 19 under high and low disease prevalence.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: serologic testing, assessment of humoral and protective immunity
Vaccine Efficacy: 100% protection against field strain B abortus-induced abortion
Immune Response: induced negative results for serologic tests, including agar gel immunodiffusion
Vaccine Introduction: The study also mentions Brucella abortus strain 19, which was less effective than strain RB51.

Title: Enzyme immunoassays for serological diagnosis of bovine brucellosis: A trial in Latin America.
Vaccine Introduction: The study reports on the performance of serological assays in detecting antibodies in cattle vaccinated with B. abortus 19.

Title: The defect in the metabolism of erythritol of the Brucella abortus B19 vaccine strain is unrelated with its attenuated virulence in mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Virulence testing, erythritol oxidation, phenotypic markers
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the B19 vaccine strain and its derivatives in relation to erythritol metabolism and virulence.

Title: Study of the resistance of rabbits immunized with combined vaccines to Brucella culture
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the resistance of rabbits immunized with combined vaccines against Brucella culture.

Title: Whole-blood lymphocyte stimulation assay for measurement of cell-mediated immune responses in bovine brucellosis.
Immune Response: Correlation between cell-mediated immune response and bacteriological findings; little correlation between immune and humoral responses among vaccinated animals
Vaccine Introduction: The study involved cattle vaccinated with Brucella abortus 19 and assessed their immune responses using a whole-blood lymphocyte stimulation assay.

Title: Effect of P39 gene deletion in live Brucella vaccine strains on residual virulence and protective activity in mice.
Extracted Vaccine Name: Brucella abortus S19, Brucella melitensis Rev.1
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Gene deletion mutants and virulence assessment
Vaccine Introduction: P39 gene deletion mutants of vaccine strains Brucella abortus S19 and Brucella melitensis Rev.1 were constructed by gene replacement.

Title: HIV peptide conjugated to heat-killed bacteria promotes antiviral responses in immunodeficient mice.
Vaccine Formulation: Heat-killed Brucella abortus conjugated to HIV peptide
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Viral neutralization studies, cytokine response measurement
Vaccine Efficacy: Induced high levels of IL-12, IFN-gamma, and IL-10; generated neutralizing antibodies against HIV
Immune Response: Production of serum IgG and IgA anti-V3 antibodies
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the use of heat-killed Brucella abortus as a carrier to enhance antiviral responses in the context of HIV infection.

Title: O-Polysaccharide epitopic heterogeneity at the surface of Brucella spp. studied by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and flow cytometry.
Immune Response: Passive protection of some MAbs against smooth Brucella infection in mice
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the O-PS epitopes on Brucella strains and the potential for developing vaccine strains devoid of specific epitopes to help differentiate infected from vaccinated animals.

Title: Safety of Brucella abortus strain RB51 in Bison.
Vaccine Formulation: 1.8 x 10(10) CFU for adult males and calves; 1 x 10(9) CFU for adult females
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Vaccination followed by necropsy and tissue culture
Vaccine Efficacy: No prolonged bacterial colonization; did not induce abortions
Immune Response: Presence of SRB51 antibodies following vaccination
Vaccine Introduction: Not reported

Title: Evaluation of lipopolysaccharides and polysaccharides of different epitopic structures in the indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for diagnosis of brucellosis in small ruminants and cattle.
Vaccine Introduction: Also mentions B. melitensis Rev 1 as a vaccine for sheep and goats.

Title: Cloning and sequencing of yajC and secD homologs of Brucella abortus and demonstration of immune responses to YajC in mice vaccinated with B. abortus RB51.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Western blot analysis, in vitro stimulation with recombinant MBP-YajC fusion protein
Immune Response: Proliferation of splenocytes and production of gamma interferon
Vaccine Introduction: The study also mentions immune responses to YajC in mice inoculated with B. abortus 19 or 2308 and B. melitensis RM1.

Title: Vaccination against bovine brucellosis with a low dose of strain 19 administered by the conjunctival route. III. -- Serological response and immunity in the pregnant cow.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Serological tests, bacteriological examination, bacterial enumeration
Vaccine Efficacy: Significantly lower degree of infection in vaccinated groups compared to controls
Immune Response: Transient rise in titers after booster vaccination
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the efficacy of Brucella abortus strain B 19 administered by the conjunctival route in heifers, comparing different vaccination schedules.

Title: Protection against infection and abortion induced by virulent challenge exposure after oral vaccination of cattle with Brucella abortus strain RB51.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Challenge exposure with virulent B abortus strain 2308
Vaccine Efficacy: Significant protection against abortion and colonization
Immune Response: Did not stimulate antibodies against the O-polysaccharide (OPS) of B abortus
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the efficacy of the oral Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine in cattle as a model for vaccination of wild ungulates.

Title: Quantitative assessment by flow cytometry of T-lymphocytes producing antigen-specific gamma-interferon in Brucella immune cattle.
Gene or Protein Antigen: cytoplasmic proteins of rough Brucella melitensis B115
Vaccine Introduction: Brucellergene is a mixture of cytoplasmic proteins of rough Brucella melitensis B115 used for stimulating immune responses in cattle.

Title: Vaccination with live Escherichia coli expressing Brucella abortus Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase protects mice against virulent B. abortus.
Vaccine Efficacy: Induced significant protection against virulent B. abortus
Immune Response: Induced antibodies to Cu/Zn SOD and strong proliferative response of splenocytes
Vaccine Introduction: B. abortus vaccine strain RB51 was mentioned as a comparison.

Title: Stimulating activity of Brucella fractions in a human lymphocyte transformation test. Correlation with humoral and cellular immunity.
Immune Response: Correlation with humoral antibodies and cutaneous response
Vaccine Introduction: Another phenol-extracted and peptidoglycan containing fraction (4A) was also used in the study.

Title: [Jet method of administration of live brucella vaccine].
Vaccine Efficacy: effective in developing stable and prolonged immunity
Vaccine Introduction: The study discusses the use of a live brucella vaccine prepared from the Br. abortus strain 19-BA and its administration via the jet method.

Title: Immunogenicity of recombinant Escherichia coli expressing the omp31 gene of Brucella melitensis in BALB/c mice.
Experiment Used to Investigate the Vacci: Immunization and challenge with smooth B. melitensis H38S
Immune Response: Induction of systemic humoral and cellular immune responses
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates a recombinant E. coli vaccine expressing the omp31 gene from Brucella melitensis.

Title: [Effect of brucellosis protective antigen on the phagocytic activity of the cells].
Vaccine Introduction: The study investigates the protective function of a protective antigen in guinea pigs against brucellosis.
